articles.title_orig: Binance Estimates $6.3 Billion Hacked in Crypto's Biggest Heist
articles.title_zh: Binance Estimates $6.3 Billion Hacked in Crypto's Biggest Heist
articles.content_orig:
Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has said that about $6.3bn in funds have been stolen in a “security incident” that looks to be the biggest crypto heist in history.
The world’s largest crypto exchange said on Thursday that it had suspended all deposits and withdrawals and that about $3bn in funds had been frozen following the apparent hacking.
Binance said an initial investigation suggested that a hacker had been able to make unauthorised transactions after gaining access to an engineer’s compromised laptop.
The company said it would cover all losses, adding that user funds were “safe”.
“Our teams are working around the clock to resolve this issue safely and thoroughly,” Binance said in a statement to Al Jazeera.
“We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice.”
The company added that it would share a “detailed” technical post-mortem once investigations were complete.
Changpeng Zhao, Binance’s founder and largest shareholder, said earlier that the exchange appeared to have been hacked.
TRM, a blockchain intelligence firm, said in a report that it assessed with “high confidence” that the attack was carried out by North Korea’s hacking unit TraderTraitor, which investigators have linked to the Lazarus Group.
Ari Redbord, TRM’s global head of policy, described the attack as “unprecedented” and a “watershed”.
“When North Korea steals at this scale, the money funds weapons proliferation and other destabilising activity. That makes this a global security issue, not just a crypto theft,” Redbord told Al Jazeera.
The price of Bitcoin, the world’s most popular cryptocurrency, fell about 5 percent following the heist, dropping below $77,000.
“Binance is one of the largest centralised exchanges, and so a blow to confidence in them risks shocking confidence to many retail investors, which could dampen prices of crypto assets,” Sean Foley, an expert in crypto markets at Macquarie University in Sydney, told Al Jazeera.
Foley said the attack highlighted the risks of centralised exchanges and could spur more traders to use decentralised alternatives.
“Any assets held at a centralised exchange are only as safe as the exchange itself, and the larger the exchange’s holdings, the larger a target it becomes,” Foley said.
The Binance hacking dwarfs the previous record for a crypto theft, set in 2025 when North Korean state-backed Lazarus Group carried out a $1.5bn heist on Bybit.
Cybercriminals stole $2.87bn in crypto assets in nearly 150 hacking incidents in 2025, according to the 2026 Crypto Crime Report produced by TRM.
Binance, founded in China by Zhao in 2017, has about $155bn in assets under management, more than any other exchange, according to CoinMarketCap.

articles.title_orig: China seeks to strengthen cooperation with Iceland in Arctic affairs
articles.title_zh: China seeks to strengthen cooperation with Iceland in Arctic affairs
articles.content_orig:
Chinese President Xi Jinping, center left and Zhang Shengmin, Vice Chairman of the Central Military Commission second from right attend a ceremony in honor of fallen national heroes at the Monument to the People's Heroes to mark Martyrs' Day at Tiananmen Square in Beijing, Wednesday, Sept. 30, 2026. Ng Han Guan/AP hide caption
BANGKOK — China's top leaders on Thursday elevated the only remaining general on the commission that oversees the country's military to the Politburo, the top governing body of the Communist Party.
The leaders also adopted a resolution on strengthening self-governance, discipline and anti-corruption in the party, as they seek to extend their grip on power.
During a four-day closed-door meeting, top Communist Party leaders deliberated on and adopted resolutions that will guide the party in the coming years. The meeting comes about a year before President Xi Jinping is widely expected to secure his fourth five-year term as the party's leader.
The party elected Gen. Zhang Shengmin, who currently serves as vice chairman of the Central Military Commission, to the Politburo. Xi had earlier purged two of China's top generals, leaving Zhang as the commission's only member besides Xi himself. It also left the Politburo without any representatives from the People's Liberation Army.
Zhang also holds a position overseeing internal discipline for the military, serving as deputy secretary of the CMC Commission for Discipline Inspection.
The party said in a summary of the resolution that the tasks facing it were "increasingly arduous," such as "uniting and leading the people to safeguard national sovereignty, security, and development interests."
It said it must step up its self-governance, which involves rooting out corruption and maintaining ideological purity.
The party should, "with an eye on enhancing its long-term governance capacity, maintain its progressive nature and purity, and its close, flesh-and-blood ties with the people," according to a summary of the resolution from the official Xinhua News Agency.
Xi has championed anti-corruption since coming to power in 2012, and has sustained a crackdown on officials for more than a decade. However, analysts say the focus now also includes underperforming officials.
Party members also reviewed the earlier purges of top members and military officials, confirming the personnel changes.
The plenum meeting revealed wider-than-expected purges, according to analysis by Neil Thomas, a senior fellow at Asia Policy who studies Chinese politics. He calculated an attendance rate of 74 percent, the lowest since the times of former leader Mao Zedong, who ran political purges regularly.

articles.title_orig: Netanyahu’s party claims election ‘stolen’ as results show him losing majority
articles.title_zh: Netanyahu’s party claims election ‘stolen’ as results show him losing majority
articles.content_orig:
Israel’s final election count left both Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc and the opposition led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot short of the 61 seats needed to form a government.
The outcome sets up weeks of coalition bargaining and political uncertainty, with the opposition alliance facing an uphill battle to assemble a majority government in the 120-seat Knesset.
Netanyahu’s Likud party and its hard-right allies won 53 seats in the Knesset, according to the Central Elections Committee, short of the 61 needed for a majority and down from 64 seats in the 2022 election.
The main opposition bloc, led by Eisenkot, won 48 seats, falling short of the 61 needed for a majority.
Eisenkot now faces a difficult coalition path. Most parties in his bloc have rejected relying on the Arab-led parties, while Eisenkot has said neither meets his conditions for a partnership. The Joint List and Ra’am won a combined 19 seats, an all-time high for Arab-led parties.
Netanyahu's party has intensified claims that the Arab-led parties "stole" the election, amplifying an allegation that spread after exit polls showed the prime minister's bloc had suffered a setback.
Likud asserted Thursday, without evidence, that foreign interference was " aimed at facilitating a foreign takeover of the Knesset , the Islamization of Israel and toppling of the right wing government."
The statement came a day after Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg, who chairs the Central Elections Committee, asked the Shin Bet security agency to investigate "serious suspicions" of improper influence through funding from foreign entities.
Sohlberg said he couldn't attest to the substance of the suspicions and directed agencies to verify the claims.
Qatar, accused of trying to mobilize Arab voters, has denied interfering in the elections , calling the allegations “ridiculous and dangerous in equal measure.”
Opposition leaders also called for a full investigation, while warning against using the allegations to cast doubt on or otherwise influence the election results.
Although the vote count is complete, the results remain subject to possible “minor corrections” before they are certified and submitted to President Isaac Herzog next Wednesday, according to the Central Elections Committee.
The new Knesset is due to be sworn in Nov. 10, while parties have until Nov. 18 to challenge the results.
A prolonged political stalemate could leave Netanyahu in office as caretaker prime minister through another round of coalition negotiations or potentially another election. A return to war with Iran also remains a key risk.
"Bibi [Netanyahu] is known as a 'comeback kid.' He did not become the longest-serving prime minister by accident," said P R Kumaraswamy, emeritus professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University, adding that he expected Netanyahu to maintain his current approach on Iran and Gaza for now.
Israeli assets have come under pressure this week with the shekel sustaining the worst intraday decline since 2023 on Wednesday before regaining ground. Tel Aviv's key benchmark stock index dropped 4.1% for the week as of Friday morning, according to LSEG data.
"We expect some near-term volatility for Israeli assets until a new government is formed and decides on fiscal consolidation and war-related spending," said Eirini Tsekeridou, a fixed-income analyst at Julius Baer. She added that Israel's economic fundamentals and monetary policy should provide support.
President Herzog will begin consulting with the competing parties next week and name the leader he believes has the best chance of forming a majority government.
Netanyahu may get the first call to kick off the 28-day process to build a coalition that can be extended by up to 14 day .
If those efforts fail, new elections will be called with Netanyahu remaining in office in the interim. The previous government-formation efforts have taken between 20 and 100 days, according to the Israel Democracy Institute .
Netanyahu could also push for a national unity government, arguing that the country should come together as it faces conflict on several fronts, though many of his opponents have ruled out such an arrangement.

articles.title_orig: Climate academic Andreas Malm barred from entering UK
articles.title_zh: Climate academic Andreas Malm barred from entering UK
articles.content_orig:
Swedish author was due to speak alongside Palestine Action co-founder at event discussing ban on the group
Andreas Malm, the climate academic and author of How to Blow Up a Pipeline, has been blocked from entering the UK before he was due to speak alongside a co-founder of the banned group Palestine Action .
Malm was told by immigration officials his presence in the UK “may not be considered to be conducive to the public good”. He said the decision was “scandalous” and urged the government to reconsider.
Malm, an associate professor of human ecology at Lund University in Sweden, was due to headline a conference organised by Tribune magazine next week on “Washington’s global reign of terror and Britain’s role in reinforcing it”.
He was due to speak alongside Huda Ammori, a co-founder of Palestine Action. They were expected to discuss the impact of the ban, including its effect on the author Sally Rooney, who has withdrawn her books from sale in the UK over her support for the group.
Rooney said the decision to ban Malm from the UK was a “sad and frightening act of cultural self-harm”.
The Tribune event was timed to coincide with the start of a supreme court challenge to the ban next Wednesday. While in London, Malm was also due to be interviewed for BBC Radio 4’s Radical With Gabriel Gatehouse programme.
Malm said: “I am deeply dismayed at this sudden ban on travelling to the UK. I have been going to the UK for decades – this is where I did my archival research for my PhD dissertation and lectured at dozens of universities and participated in even more conferences.”
Malm urged the government to think again. He said: “One was under the impression that the Burnham government had slightly more respect for the basic notions of freedom of expression and other democratic rights. I appeal for this decision to be overturned.”
The Home Office said it did not discuss individual cases.
Rooney said: “Andreas Malm is among the most brilliant and influential intellectuals working in Europe today. For the UK government to deny him entry to Britain is not only an outrageous attack on a respected climate expert, but a sad and frightening act of cultural self-harm.”
Earlier this year, the US leftwing commentators Cenk Uygur and Hasan Piker were also barred from the UK on the same grounds that their presence in the UK “may not be conducive to the public good”.
Tribune’s editor, Oliver Eagleton, said: “Ironically, Andreas was coming to London to speak at our event about the unprecedented attacks on free speech unleashed by the proscription of Palestine Action, including the effective ban on Sally Rooney’s books, but he has now been banned himself.
“He is being censored for speaking out about censorship, in truly Orwellian fashion. It is shameful that Andy Burnham’s government is continuing the authoritarian overreach we saw under Keir Starmer, and in this dystopian new reality it is now commonplace in Britain for authors and academics to be treated as terrorists because they support Palestinians facing genocide and the rights of people protesting that genocide.”
Malm’s books have won international awards and inspired many to take action for environmental justice and Palestinian rights. How to Blow Up a Pipeline inspired a film of the same name. He has travelled regularly to Britain to lecture at universities including Oxford, King’s College London and Cambridge.

articles.title_orig: Crypto giant Binance hit by 'largest hack in history'
articles.title_zh: Crypto giant Binance hit by 'largest hack in history'
articles.content_orig:
Binance is the world's biggest cryptocurrency trading platform
Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that $6.3bn (Â£4.7bn) of digital assets have been impacted by what could be the largest hack in history.
The world's biggest crypto exchange said about half of those assets have been frozen with the help of other platforms, adding that it will "cover all losses".
Early checks show the incident may have involved an engineer's laptop that had been compromised, which allowed an attacker to make unauthorised withdrawals, Binance said.
Two analytics firms have attributed the incident, which eclipses a record-setting $1.5bn hack on the Bybit exchange in 2025 , to a North Korean hacking unit called TraderTraitor.
AI-powered investigations company TRM Labs said in a report that several elements of the Binance attack resemble earlier North Korean-linked incidents, including the Bybit hack.
The lab's global head of policy Ari Redbord told the BBC the Binance hack is a "watershed moment" that is unlike anything the industry has seen.
The attacker still holds an enormous sum of stolen assets, meaning efforts to trace and recover the funds are far from over, Redbord added.
Chainalysis, another crypto analytics firm, also said it has "high confidence" that the North Korean group are linked to the hack.
Eric Jardine, Chainalysis' Head of Research, urged every exchange to remain vigilant as the platforms are attractive targets for hackers due to the sheer value of assets.
Binance did not directly respond to BBC queries about the incident's potential links to North Korea but said: "We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice."
The incident concerns Binance.com - while much smaller crypto platform Binance.US, which provides trading services specifically for American residents - said its platform is not affected by the issue.
Yi He is Binance's co-chief executive
In a series of posts, Yi He, Binance's co-chief executive, thanked various cryptocurrency issuers for freezing the assets.
"Safety first: withdrawals are currently disabled until the environment is confirmed to be secure," she said.
Two other major crypto platforms, Tether and Circle, said they have frozen a total of about $2.4bn of assets in response to the potential Binance hack.
Circle chief executive Jeremy Allaire said his firm is "closely tracking reports of a potential exploit involving Binance" and that his company has frozen more than $800m in assets linked to the incident.
Circle is the issuer and co-creator of the USDC, one of the world's largest US dollar-backed cryptocurrencies.
Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said his firm has frozen around $1.6bn "related to a potential Binance exchange hack."
"Protecting the industry and our partners is our main priority," said Ardoino, whose company issues a cryptocurrency known as USDT.
World Liberty Financial, a crypto company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said it has worked with its partners to freeze stolen funds.
Crypto exchange Coinbase said it was unaffected by the incident and was monitoring the situation.
Several crypto industry observers had flagged concerns about a potential hack on Binance hours before the exchange confirmed the security issue.
Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide.
The exchange has been subject of regulatory scrutiny around the world.
The company said in 2024 that it has more than $160bn in assets under custody.
Bitcoin dropped by more than 4% following the alerts. The price of other major cryptocurrencies including Ethereum and Solana also fell sharply.

articles.title_orig: Blockchain analysis firm TRM says North Korea behind Binance crypto theft
articles.title_zh: Blockchain analysis firm TRM says North Korea behind Binance crypto theft
articles.content_orig:
Hackers stole over $6 billion in cryptocurrency on Thursday, shattering the record for the largest such heist as multiple investigators pointed the finger at North Korea.
As of Thursday night in the US, a team of cryptocurrency firms had managed to freeze about $3 billion of the stolen loot amid a frenetic battle with the hackers to find and control the digital money.
The hackers broke into digital wallets held at Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange.
Binance said late Thursday that its initial investigation indicates that the hack went through an engineer’s laptop, “which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions.”
Binance said it would “cover all losses” from “the company’s funds” and an emergency assets fund, adding “user funds are safe.” The crypto exchange also said it had “temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while security checks are completed; revoked the affected address authorization; [and] engaged law enforcement and blockchain intelligence partners to trace and recover funds.”
Analysts were shocked by the amount of money impacted.
“It’s the biggest hack in history,” Aravind Srinivasan, head of large crypto market maker GSR’s systematic OTC business, told Reuters.
Crypto-tracing firm TRM Labs attributed the heist to an elite North Korean hacking unit, “based on robust on and off-chain intelligence.”
Pangolin Intelligence, another blockchain-tracking firm based in Singapore, said it also believed that a North Korean hacking unit was behind the heist.
“Analyzing the on-chain activity related to this hack and correlating with information gathered from previous known incidents [involving the North Korean cyber unit]” led to the attribution, said an analyst with Pangolin Intelligence, who did not want to be named for privacy reasons.
“I think the cat and mouse game has barely begun yet,” the Pangolin Intelligence analyst told CNN, adding that North Korea was likely poised to tap a network of money laundering organizations to try to cash out the stolen funds.
Chainalysis, another crypto-tracking company, said it was monitoring stolen funds “moving across multiple blockchains,” including Bitcoin and Ethereum. A Chainalysis spokesperson told CNN the firm had “high confidence” North Korea was behind the hack.
CNN has reached out to North Korea’s mission at the UN for comment. Pyongyang has previously denied hacking allegations.
CNN has requested comment from the FBI, as well as the US Secret Service, which also investigates cybercrime. In past investigations of big crypto hacks, the FBI has had an on-call team of analysts that worked to freeze some of the money.
If North Korea is proven to be the culprit, it would be little surprise to US law enforcement officials and private experts. North Korean hackers were blamed for the previous record-high crypto hack, when they allegedly stole $1.5 billion from Bybit, another major cryptocurrency exchange. In that case, the attackers stole an amount equal to a significant portion of North Korea’s reported annual gross domestic product in a matter of minutes.
North Korea’s formidable hacking teams are a key source of revenue for the nuclear-armed, sanctions-battered regime, according to current and former US and South Korean officials. Pyongyang-linked hackers have stolen billions of dollars from banks and cryptocurrency firms in the last several years, according to reports from the United Nations and private firms.
A 2023 CNN investigation spotlighted how the South Korean intelligence service worked with private crypto-tracking experts to seize about $1 million in cryptocurrency that North Koreans had stolen from a victim.
Unlike platforms for trading stocks, cryptocurrency exchanges tend to hold digital assets on their users’ behalf, which make them more vulnerable to hackers and theft, particularly given a lack of regulatory oversight within the relatively nascent industry.
Binance was co-founded in 2017 by Canadian national Changpeng Zhao, becoming the world’s largest crypto trading platform within a year of its launch.
However, Zhao stepped down in 2023 after pleading guilty to violating anti-money laundering laws in the US. He was sentenced to four months in federal prison, and was pardoned by President Donald Trump in October last year.
Zhao, who no longer manages the platform but remains its largest shareholder, said on X that the incident appeared to be a hack and that he expects user funds to be fully covered by the exchange.
Prices of Bitcoin and Ether, the most widely-traded cryptocurrencies, plummeted following news of the Binance breach, but regained some losses to trade about 2-3% lower midday Friday in Hong Kong.
The is a breaking news story, more to come.

articles.title_orig: Asia Stocks Under Pressure, Haven Bid Boosts Bonds: Markets Wrap
articles.title_zh: Asia Stocks Under Pressure, Haven Bid Boosts Bonds: Markets Wrap
articles.content_orig:
TOKYO – Asian shares were trading mixed Friday, as worries about the future of artificial intelligence grew after Alphabet's stock drop dragged on U.S. markets.
Japan's benchmark Nikkei 225 dropped 2.3% in afternoon trading to 63,155.94. At the end of its two-day monetary policy board meeting, the Bank of Japan decided to keep its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 1.25%. That was widely expected because the central bank raised the rate last month.
The U.S. has been pressuring Japan to raise rates because of concerns about the weakening yen. In currency trading, the U.S. dollar inched up to 157.67 Japanese yen from 157.65 yen. The euro cost $1.1186, up from $1.1181.
Australia's S&P/ASX 200 rose 0.2% to 8,908.10. South Korea's Kospi declined nearly 4% to 5,701.71, as shares in SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics both slipped.
Shares related to the great market interest in AI have tended to be volatile, because some issues, including chip makers, get pushed up because of that interest, but then may decline because of worries about supplies, for instance.
Hong Kong's Hang Seng added 1.7% to 23,359.06, while the Shanghai Composite lost 0.4% to 3,636.60.
On Wall Street, the S&P 500 fell 0.3% for its first loss in four days , even though the wide majority of stocks rose within the index and across Wall Street. The Nasdaq composite tumbled 1.4%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 132 points, or 0.3%.
Alphabet is one of the most influential stocks on Wall Street because it’s one of the largest, and the Class A shares of its stock fell 12.6% for their worst day since they began trading more than 20 years ago.
All told, the S&P 500 fell 23.59 points to 7,720.39 Thursday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 132.54 to 52,342.56, and the Nasdaq composite tumbled 365.13 to 26,184.72.
In the bond market, the yield on the 10-year Treasury fell to 4.94% from 5.05% late Wednesday. It’s been generally pulling back since it topped 5.30% earlier this month and touched its highest level since 2002.
In energy trading, benchmark U.S. crude gained 1.15% to $103.17 a barrel. Brent crude, the international standard, edged up 1.05% to $116.09 a barrel.
AP Business Writer Stan Choe contributed to this report.

Watered-down version of statement to be issued at end of Montreal summit instead offers ‘ever closer association’
The EU has backed away from its offer to Canada to start talks on becoming an “associate member” after disagreements between member states just as an EU-Canada summit was set to begin in Montreal.
A draft of a joint statement to be issued after the end of the summit, which runs Thursday and Friday, showed a watered-down version offering “an ever closer association of Canada to the EU, short of full membership itself”.
The issue was triggered after the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen , surprised nearly everyone by announcing in last month’s state of the union address that the EU would consider “associate membership” for Canada.
The declaration had been hailed as a landmark in EU history, offering a non-EU country such close ties to the bloc, which has not allowed any state membership since Croatia joined in 2013.
It was also seen as a sign that the call by Canada’s prime minister, Mark Carney , at the Davos summit in January for “middle powers” to work together was paying off.
But instead of announcing a work programme on developing “associate membership”, the draft communique, seen by the Guardian, states the two sides would “work to define by the 2027 EU-Canada summit the concept of an ever closer association of Canada to the EU, short of full membership itself, to reflect, through this even closer association, our common endeavour and cooperation towards our shared goals of prosperity, economic security and strategic autonomy”.
Associate membership had been mooted, and rejected, previously for countries such as Ukraine.
Von der Leyen’s declaration caught EU capitals by surprise and led to pushback politically and legally. Given “associate status” has no definition, diplomats wondered about such issues as whether Canada could join the European Council, legislative bodies or decision-making processes without a vote.
At a meeting on Monday, ambassadors in the EU raised concerns about the dramatic offer, but vowed to make efforts to seek a diplomatic path to rescinding the offer of “associate” membership without embarrassing Von der Leyen. It is understood that Italy suggested “associate membership as proposed by the commission”, with the definition to be thrashed out later by member states.
Germany walked back further, suggesting the wording “an ever closer association of Canada” to the EU.
“Nobody was consulted about associate membership apart from [Von der Leyen’s] closest staff, it would seem. Many member states, including Germany, were not happy. This is all about fixing the plane while it is flying,” said one diplomat.
Germany had argued that “associate membership” should be reserved as an interim step for prospective candidate countries, such as Ukraine or Montenegro, noting that the status has no formal grounding in current EU treaties.
Donald Trump, the US president, previously called the EU’s proposal to make Canada an associate member “laughable”, and said if he ​interpreted the move as a “hostile act” the US might stop trading with Europe “on many things”.
A bitter trade war with the US, a longtime ally, has seen Carney seek out new trading partnerships around the world. Ahead of the summit in Montreal, one of Canada’s largest banks released a report suggesting there was “meaningful” upside for Canada if it were to deepen economic ties with Europe. Tens of billions of dollars in additional trade would be possible if barriers were removed in areas of overlapping interest such as defence, energy, critical minerals and digital markets, TD Economics said .
Carney has spoken specifically about the need to lessen reliance on Elon Musk‘s Starlink satellite network, following a decision to throttle its usage over Ukraine.
Earlier this week, Carney posted on social media that Canada would join the popular music competition Eurovision. But despite fears raised by political rivals, Carney has said Canada has no interest in formally joining the EU. Changing Canadian laws to bring it in line with European nations would probably prove unpopular, despite public support for stronger ties.
Carney told reporters on Tuesday that the summit this week was the launch of further formal negotiations that will take place another year.
“The good news is it doesn’t matter about ⁠specific names or nomenclature,” Carney said. “What matters is the difference it will ​make to the lives ​of Canadians.”
A previous draft statement ​had included at least two references to Canada as an “associate member”, ​including an acknowledgment that ‌defining the ​term would take ​another year.

articles.title_orig: China Elevates Key Figure in Purges With Rare Politburo Pick
articles.title_zh: China Elevates Key Figure in Purges With Rare Politburo Pick
articles.content_orig:
The unprecedented number of empty seats at the fifth plenum – a symbol of expulsions – serve as a symbol for the scale of the purges under Xi Jinping
China expelled a record number of officials from the Chinese Communist party (CCP) as it concluded a major political gathering , which saw an unprecedented number of empty seats indicating the scale of the purges under Xi Jinping.
A record 33 members were expelled at this week’s fifth plenum, a gathering of top officials that takes place roughly once a year.
Just 279 of the full and alternate members of the CCP’s Central Committee attended this week’s gathering, compared with the 376 originally named as members in 2022. That means that more than 25% of the original cohort were absent, many due to purges. It is the highest number of “empty chairs” at the plenum in modern Chinese history.
The confirmed expulsions included Zhang Youxia, the former second-in-command to China’s leader in the military hierarchy, and Ma Xingrui, the former party secretary for Xinjiang. Other absences were unexplained.
“More empty seats underscores the plenum’s focus on Xi’s vision of strict internal discipline,” said Neil Thomas, a senior fellow at the Asia Society thinktank, in a post on X.
The theme for this week’s plenum was party governance. Since coming to power in 2012 Xi has focused on stamping out corruption in the party. But in recent years the campaign has intensified , taking out officials in the highest ranks of the party and the military, raising questions about if the campaign is also a tool to remove political rivals or punish disloyalty.
Xi appears to have grown increasingly frustrated with what he sees as a lack of discipline in the ranks of the party that wields absolute authority over the state and society in China. Earlier this year he said that the party must uproot “sick trees” and that the fight against corruption was a “never-ending journey”.
A series of purges has gutted the seven-man Central Military Commission, the ruling body of China’s People’s Liberation Army. There are now just two members left: Xi himself, and the military’s anti-graft tsar, Zhang Shengmin.
Zhang was promoted to the politburo of the CCP this week, the highest ruling body in the party. Zhang is now the only military member of the senior leadership body.
The plenum also laid the groundwork for the 21st Party congress, an event which happens every five years and is expected to next be held in the second half of 2027. Xi is expected to secure a fourth term as leader of the party, making him the longest ruler of Communist China since Mao Zedong.
The ranks of the Central Committee and the politburo will be refreshed at next year’s congress, but many analysts believe that recent purges have been so wide-ranging that there are few suitable candidates to be promoted.

articles.title_orig: European Central Bank head resigns, allowing EU leaders to choose successor before French election
articles.title_zh: European Central Bank head resigns, allowing EU leaders to choose successor before French election
articles.content_orig:
European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said on Thursday she had decided to step down eight months before her term was due to expire so that she can speak more freely on issues beyond monetary policy.
Lagarde, 70, has led the ECB since November 2019 and previously headed the International Monetary Fund. Her term would otherwise have run until October 2027.
“There is never a good time to leave,” Lagarde told a press conference. “But it’s embedded in the governance of the ECB that presidents, board members have to leave because they cannot be up for renewal.”
Lagarde said the decision to leave early was driven by a wish to engage on issues outside the ECB’s mandate.
“I want to have the freedom of speech, the freedom of expression and the freedom to engage on matters that are not monetary policy matters,” she said.
She noted that ECB officials are bound by strict rules of neutrality: “We have an obligation of neutrality, we comment on the situation with the focus on monetary policy,” Lagarde said, adding that the mandate is “the price we pay for being independent.”
Lagarde said she no longer felt comfortable staying silent on broader global issues. “I’m interested in the truth, and I see the truth being very often damaged, contradicted by misrepresentation,” she said, without elaborating.
Drawing on more than two decades in international economic and financial roles, Lagarde said she believed she had something to contribute beyond central banking. “There are things that I can say — whether people will listen or not is another story. But I feel that I should say those things and I cannot do so in my current position,” she said.
Lagarde sought to reassure markets and staff that her early departure would not disrupt the central bank’s operations. “A process has already started to identify my successor,” she said, adding there were “plenty of excellent candidates — much better than me, actually.”
She dismissed concerns about continuity. “Don’t worry about decision making in limbo — no, absolutely not,” Lagarde said. “The institution is solid, strong, like a rock, and it will continue being so.”

articles.title_orig: Resonance of Fate 4K/HD Edition to receive an 'Enhanced Remaster' DLC, adding HDR, 120FPS, 2x speed mode, & more (Update)
articles.title_zh: Resonance of Fate 4K/HD Edition to receive an 'Enhanced Remaster' DLC, adding HDR, 120FPS, 2x speed mode, & more (Update)
articles.content_orig:
Tri-Ace has officially announced Resonance of Fate Enhanced Remaster , now available for PlayStation 5 and PC ( Steam ). The PlayStation 5 version will be priced at $34.99, while the PC upgrade will be priced at $9.99. Those who own the PS4 version of Resonance of Fate 4K/HD on PlayStation Network can also upgrade for $9.99.
The listing for the Enhanced Remaster can be found below.
In the far distant future, humanity clings to existence on a ravaged earth on the brink of collapse. Their only hope for survival lies in ‘Basel’, a huge machine that controls the environment. The story beings as the gears continue to spin, humanity is led by a ruling class, which the heroes support as mercenaries.
The fate of the world hangs in the balance as you progress through the many gun fights.
Resonance of Fate was originally published in 2010 and remastered in 2018 as 4K/HD Editon.
This Enhanced Remaster further expands the graphics options, including native 4K output and HDR support. Traverse this haunted world while getting involved in numerous gun fights, now in even higher-quality, higher-resolution visuals.
The steampunk aesthetic, fateful story, soaring symphonic soundtrack, and intense gun combat for which the game is known now burst to life and play out with even more beautiful graphics.
All the action is set to a magnificent music score composed by Motoi Sakuraba and Kohei Tanaka.
Experience the story of destiny more deeply and vividly than ever before.
A new DLC listing for Resonance of Fate 4K/HD Edition has appeared on Steam, called the Resonance of Fate/End of Eternity Enhanced Remaster . It it set to release on October 29.
According to the listing, it offers new graphics options for the game, including native 4K output, HDR, and 120FPS support. It will also upscale textures and add a 2x game speed feature.
Although details are sparse, hopefully this DLC will be an optional free download, similar to the High Resolution Texture Pack that originally launched alongside the 4K/Edition in 2018.
Resonance of Fate 4K/HD Edition is a 2018 remaster of 2010's Resonance of Fate , originally published by Sega and developed by Tri-Ace ( Star Ocean series).
Thanks to the eagle-eyed Wario64 for the spot.
Resonance of Fate/End of Eternity 4K/HD Edition returns with even more enhancements as the Enhanced Remaster!
This content significantly expands the available graphics options, including native 4K output, HDR, and support for 120 fps.
In addition, the character and environment textures have been upscaled, bringing an even more detailed and beautiful world to life.
A new 2x Game Speed feature has also been added, allowing you to enjoy the game at a more comfortable pace.
A story of firearms and bonds set on a devastated Earth.
Enjoy this “gunplay symphony RPG,” combining stylish battles where you soar through the air and unleash a barrage of shots with deep strategic gameplay, now with enhanced visuals and an improved play experience.

articles.title_orig: Chinese Embassy in Mexico slams US officials’ malicious smears against China-Mexico cooperation
articles.title_zh: Chinese Embassy in Mexico slams US officials’ malicious smears against China-Mexico cooperation
articles.content_orig:
WASHINGTON — A top aide to U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro said in a phone call Monday night that prosecutors had made a “f---up” in a high-profile criminal case against two former FBI officials , an agent who’s been investigating the case testified Thursday.
The former officials, Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, were initially charged last week with making false statements to Congress about their level of knowledge about an investigation of Hunter Biden’s laptop.
A sworn affidavit attached to the complaint by Special Agent Ryan Witt cited a congressional staffer who was present for both Floris’ and Benavides’ testimony — but it turns out the person was only present for Benavides’, Witt testified at a preliminary hearing on whether there’s probable cause to charge the pair.
Witt told Magistrate Judge Zia M. Faruqui that he called the congressional staffer on Monday and was later joined on the call by Pirro aide Carlton Davis and Pirro, the top federal prosecutor for Washington, D.C.
Audio of that conversation was turned over to Benavides’ attorney, Ron Safer, who read parts of the exchange in court and asked Witt whether it was accurate.
At one point, Davis told the staffer, House Judiciary Committee general counsel Steve Castor, “This is our f---up,” and asked for his help finding someone who had been present for the testimony, Witt confirmed.
Witt added that he still has not been able to speak to anyone who was there.
Later Monday night, prosecutors filed what they called a superseding criminal complaint and a new affidavit, neither of which was signed by any law enforcement officer or judge. Faruqui tossed the complaint on Tuesday.
On Wednesday, one of the attorneys for the defense asked Witt if it was unusual for a case alleging defendants made false statements to use an affidavit containing false statements — a question the judge cut off.
Davis, who is listed as a special counsel in Pirro’s office, was involved in the failed effort to indict six sitting members of Congress over their comments in a social media video where they urged members of the military not to follow illegal orders. Davis previously worked as a Republican staffer on several committees, including the House Select Committee on Benghazi.
Witt was on the stand in the case for a third day.
He testified Tuesday that he was assigned to the case in July after FBI Director Kash Patel sent a letter directing the Kansas City, Missouri, office to look into certain people, including Floris.
The direction came a day after President Donald Trump delivered an Oval Office address in which he complained that “rogue bureaucrats” had suppressed information about China’s efforts to interfere in the 2020 election, which he falsely claims was “stolen.”
Both Floris and Benavides were involved in FBI efforts to secure the election and have long been targets of criticism from Trump’s allies.
Witt said he was unhappy with the assignment, in part because “I had concerns that this would be viewed as political.”
Witt said Wednesday that top FBI brass, including Patel, had been checking on progress in the case through in-person meetings, videoconferences and updates pushed through their special agent in charge. Witt said both FBI deputy directors — Chris Raia and Andrew Bailey, who recently resigned — were involved.
“The evidence in this case speaks for itself [as] to the effect that kind of pressure has on sensitive investigations like this one,” Floris’ attorney Mary Dohrmann told the judge Thursday.
She said there were other mistakes in the affidavit as well, and that some of the false statements her client was alleged to have made were presented stripped of necessary context.
Safer, Benavides’ attorney, told Faruqui that in most instances, calling something a political prosecution is a talking point, but not in this case.
“That is the price we pay to allow politics to infect the process,” he said.
The judge said he plans to issue a written ruling Monday morning.
Ryan J. Reilly is a justice reporter for NBC News.
Tanish Bijur is an intern on the Justice and National Security Unit
Dareh Gregorian is a politics reporter for NBC News.

articles.title_orig: Latest Gemini design comes to all Android devices, app upgrades file generation
articles.title_zh: Latest Gemini design comes to all Android devices, app upgrades file generation
articles.content_orig:
A pair of Gemini app updates today brings the latest design to all Android devices, while file generation sees a big upgrade.
The latest Gemini overlay design applies a heavy blur effect over the bar. It’s hard to make out the boundaries of the pill, while there are way more tiny specks and swirls of color. Once the animations complete, you can see how the pill-shaped bar is translucent at the perimeter instead of a solid shape.
This updated design was first introduced on phones with Gemini Intelligence (Pixel 11) and is now available on all other devices we checked today. Make sure to Force stop the Google app if you’re not seeing it yet.
Meanwhile, the Gemini app now lets you “generate, preview, and edit files right within” chats. You can have Gemini create a text document, presentation, or spreadsheet about a specific topic and then view it inline. Highlight sections to make edits or ask questions.
PDF preview and editing are supported on gemini.google.com and the mobile apps, while Google Docs, Google Sheets, Google Slides, Markdown files, TXT files, and code are web-only.
File creation and editing are live for “users in all languages where the Gemini app is available.”

articles.title_orig: Canada and Europe share challenge of diversifying without antagonizing US and China
articles.title_zh: Canada and Europe share challenge of diversifying without antagonizing US and China
articles.content_orig:
MONTREAL — There’s one thing the European Union and Canada want to avoid with their new alliance: stoking new fury from Washington and Beijing.
Officials have been under pressure to check off everything they said they would do at the last summit and on Friday will unveil the areas they plan to focus on over the next year, as they intensify their transatlantic cooperation. But don’t expect a parade of new deals.
“Canada has objectives where they need our technology — so you can build a beautiful relationship if you focus on it,” one senior EU official told POLITICO about shared challenges in diversifying away from the U.S. and China. The official was granted anonymity to speak candidly about sensitive diplomatic negotiations between Brussels and Ottawa.
One of the core EU interests in Canada, the official explained, is a chance for the bloc to diversify its supply of critical raw materials and sources of energy to further reduce its dependence on China and Russia, respectively.
“They have most of what we need,” the official said about Canadian minerals. “There’s also a huge opportunity to bring Canadian fossil fuels and gas to the EU.”
Prime Minister Mark Carney dismissed the controversy over whether the EU should label the relationship with Canada as an “associate membership,” saying on Thursday it was a sideshow to what’s been billed as a landmark summit.
Earlier this week, Germany, France, Greece and other countries opposed the definition in a joint EU-Canada statement to be issued in Montreal. That came after European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen put forward the “associate membership” label in September.
But Carney told reporters on Thursday that the new alliance wasn’t “a marketing exercise” and that the name doesn’t matter. “What matters is that the complementarities of our two jurisdictions strengthen our sovereignty, strengthen Europe’s sovereignty, various strategic autonomies, critical minerals, energy, other aspects — AI,” he said.
A tricky political road lies ahead as Carney and von der Leyen make moves to draw the EU and Canada closer in a partnership that doesn’t include its southern neighbor. They’ll need to  tiptoe forward with an “association without accession” work plan in the last years of the U.S. President Donald Trump’s time in office.
Montreal’s historic Fairmont The Queen Elizabeth hotel was a hub of summit activity on Thursday, beginning with a morning spectacle of von der Leyen heading out of the hotel in runners, taking staff out for a walking meeting. EU commissioners and Canadian Cabinet ministers sailed in and out of the hotel’s perfumed lobby, greeting colleagues.
Jet-lagged Europeans, along with Canadian officials and lobbyists, commiserated over what they saw as poor summit organization, spread across multiple locations.
The debate over membership semantics became a luncheon laugh line when European Council President António Costa endorsed Von der Leyen’s offer to Canada before joking the final designation is “subject to revision”
Then, between servings of frisée salad and roast salmon, Costa struck a diplomatic balance.
“Tomorrow, the European Union and Canada will launch an alliance for the future of Europe,” he said, invoking German Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s preferred label and a term Carney has also used to describe the relationship. But Costa also backed von der Leyen’s “ambition” of Canada as an “associate member” of the EU, admitting the term might not matter in the end.
By mid-afternoon, Carney seemed to come around to the term, recognizing the work underway to deepen relations as “an alliance for the future, with Canada as an associate member, between Canada and the European Union.”
The two sides are expected to announce a wrap on talks on a new digital trade agreement on Friday, ending negotiations that were launched in the spring. Other anticipated outcomes include an agreement between the European Investment Bank and Canada, geared to allow the bloc to fund Canadian critical minerals projects.
Eleven EU commissioners in town to “further an agenda” is no small accomplishment, Canadian Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne told reporters. “It’s a historic moment that we need to seize.”
AI and energy companies are expected to be major beneficiaries of an enhanced EU–Canada relationship, making the absences of European Energy Commissioner Dan Jørgensen and Canadian Energy and Natural Resources Minister Tim Hodgson noteworthy.
Zoya Sheftalovich contributed to this report from Montreal.

articles.title_orig: Israel’s final election results show neither Netanyahu nor rival can immediately form government
articles.title_zh: Israel’s final election results show neither Netanyahu nor rival can immediately form government
articles.content_orig:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ’s right-wing bloc won 53 seats in Israel’s 120-member Knesset, or parliament, results released by election officials on Thursday showed, well below the 68 it had controlled at its peak in the previous parliament.
The bloc supporting Netanyahu’s main rival, Gadi Eisenkot , won 48 seats in an extremely tight election race , meaning neither secured the 61 seats needed to form a government.
The count is complete, but the results still need to be certified and submitted to President Isaac Herzog next Wednesday.
Herzog will then consult with party chairs and choose a candidate ⁠who he thinks has the best chance to form a government.
Parties led by Israel’s Arab minority made historic gains, winning a combined 19 seats in a race in which Palestinians with Israeli citizenship headed to the polls in record numbers Tuesday, many hoping to oust Netanyahu and far-right members of his coalition, including Bezalel Smotrich, his finance minister, and National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir.
Both leading blocs have ruled out the possibility of forming a government with the two main Arab parties, Ra’am and the Joint List. But their rise as potential kingmakers has brought the complex realities faced by Palestinian Israeli nationals into fresh focus.
Ahead of the election, Netanyahu and other members of his coalition amplified allegations of foreign election interference , referring Arab parties to the domestic security service, the Shin Bet, for investigation over allegations of Qatari intervention.
Qatar denied the allegations. Mansour Abbas, the head of Ra’am, said his party had “no connection” to such conduct and urged a full investigation. He also accused Netanyahu of a “campaign of incitement and delegitimization ” against Arab citizens.
Dean Livne, the acting director general of Israel’s Central Elections Committee, said in a published letter sent to a member of parliament that there was “no basis for allegations of systematic violations of electoral integrity.”
Before the election, both Netanyahu and Eisenkot ruled out forming a government with the Arab parties.
But Yair Golan, the head of the smaller left-wing Democrats party, called for a government formed “in partnership” with Arab parties. “We must no longer accept Netanyahu’s racist division between Jewish votes and Arab votes,” he said Wednesday on X.
The majority of Palestinians with Israeli citizenship are the descendants of those who remained within what became Israel during the war that led to the country’s founding in 1948. At the time, hundreds of thousands more fled or were expelled from their homes.
Chantal Da Silva reports on world news for NBC News Digital and is based in London.

articles.title_orig: 3 customers suffer chemical burns after drinking margaritas at Chili's in North Carolina
articles.title_zh: 3 customers suffer chemical burns after drinking margaritas at Chili's in North Carolina
articles.content_orig:
by Marisa Sardonia & Marc Liverman
FOREST CITY, N.C. (WLOS) — An investigation is underway after a chemical exposure incident at a Chili's Grill & Bar in western North Carolina, officials confirmed.
The incident led to multiple people enduring chemical burns after consuming drinks that were prepared with a cleaning chemical mistakenly identified as sugar, according to a press release from the Foothills Health District. This occurred at the restaurant's Forest City location.
The Foothills Health District said preliminary information indicates that on Monday, Oct. 26, an employee received a "granulated degreasing chemical" from a contracted worker power-washing the outside of the restaurant and put it in an unlabeled container. The container was then brought into the restaurant and left in the bar area, the public health agency said.
On Wednesday, Oct. 28, an employee preparing the bar for lunch service found the container and used it to prepare margaritas, believing it was sugar.
According to the release, three customers later ordered margaritas and "immediately experienced discomfort" and had chemical burns in and around their mouths, before telling staff of the situation and leaving to seek medical attention. In response, two restaurant employees tasted the substance in the container and had similar symptoms, per preliminary findings.
"I'm not sure what degree of chemical burns they had, but they went to urgent care and were treated there," Foothills Health District spokesperson Megan Rollins said.
The Foothills Health District then opened an investigation and issued an immediate suspension of the food service permit at the Chili's location. Staff were instructed to thoroughly wash and sanitize affected food preparation areas, as well as equipment and surfaces.
Levonne Baker, a regular Chili's customer, spoke to News13 about the incident.
"I was beyond surprised and almost scared," Baker said.
He described the situation as something out of a horror movie.
Baker says the incident has also made him reconsider whether he will return to the restaurant's bar.
"It has made me a little nervous about going back to the bar because it's like what's in there next? I mean, am I going to be the next person who's going next door? And not for an oil change," he said.
Both a vehicle mechanic and an urgent care are located right next to the restaurant.
As of Thursday morning, environmental health specialists with Foothills Health District have completed their investigation. The food service permit at the Chili's location has also been reinstated after officials determined the restaurant met "all applicable food safety requirements."
The restaurant chain was contacted for comment but had not responded at the time of the report.
Health officials say the incident highlights the importance of properly labeling chemicals in workplaces and homes to prevent accidental exposure.
Rollins added that by having everything labeled, if something is still ingested, it can be easier to identify.
“Then you can call poison control, and they can walk you through exactly how to neutralize that chemical," Rollins said.
Anyone who experiences symptoms after a suspected chemical exposure can contact Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 for guidance.

articles.title_orig: Ghostty 1.4 is out with big improvements on Linux
articles.title_zh: Ghostty 1.4 is out with big improvements on Linux
articles.content_orig:
A major new release of Ghostty , the open-source terminal emulator, is out.
Ghostty 1.4.0 brings a varied set of changes after seven months of development. There are welcome performance optimisations on Linux and macOS, a more capable SSH implementation and an easier way to rearrange tab splits – dragging them!
This update to the Zig-based app offers complete Kitty graphics protocol support (including animation and relative placements) – the first terminal besides Kitty to do so. If you use TUI tools or script to render images in the terminal, this is a major feat.
Devs say performance is improved hugely with this update. Notably, Ghostty 1.4.0 now compresses off-screen scrollback when the terminal is idle. This lowers the amount of physical RAM used by text-heavy histories by up to 90%.
Content is decompressed if you scroll back or you make use of the text search feature that was added in the Ghostty 1.3.0 update earlier this year.
On Linux, Ghostty’s GTK app renders text sharply at fractional display scales such as 125% and 150%, which should resolve oft-mentioned issues with blurry text.
The update also replaces GtkGLArea with an EGL rendering pipeline that runs on a separate thread and passes frames to GTK using DMA-BUFs. This requires a system EGL library; if a GPU can’t export DMA-BUFs, slower CPU-based copying is used.
And terminal splits in the GTK build can be rearranged using drag. When a tab has two or more splits, each split has a drag handle that can be grabbed and the split dragged and dropped onto another split.
And configuration options on GTK builds include gtk-horizontal-tab-scroll , which can be set to false to disable two-finger scrolling from changing tabs, and gtk-tabs-inverted , to move the close button to the start of each tab.
Ubuntu 26.10 includes Ghostty in the repos , putting it an apt install ghostty away. But, that won’t get you the newest version. For the changes mentioned above, you’ll need to use an alternative method.
You can install Ghostty on Ubuntu using an unofficial community-maintained Ghostty DEB (and that has its own Ghostty PPA for easy updates). There’s also a Ghostty AppImage , and an unofficial Snap .
On macOS, Ghostty provides official binaries (recommended; supports in-app updating), and it’s also available via Homebrew and other CLI package managers.
As Ghostty 1.4.0 requires GTK 4.18 and libadwaita 1.7, per the terminal’s GTK/Adwaita version policy , Ubuntu 24.04 LTS no longer meets the requirements. This means a DEB version of Ghostty (e.g. from the PPA above) can no longer be installed.
As an aside, the underlying libghostty terminal emulation library will be powering terminals in future versions of JetBrains’ IDEs . Linux Mint’s new terminal app, Velocitty , doesn’t use that, but its design is said to have been inspired by Ghostty .

articles.title_orig: Crypto firms freeze more than $2.5bn in funds as Binance investigates potential hack
articles.title_zh: Crypto firms freeze more than $2.5bn in funds as Binance investigates potential hack
articles.content_orig:
World’s largest crypto exchange said it had not confirmed whether funds had been pilfered
Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, said on Thursday it is investigating reports of a potential security issue as its founder said the incident “does look like a hack on Binance”. The company said cryptocurrency firms had frozen about $3bn in funds by Thursday evening.
It was not immediately clear the extent of the damage hackers might have been able to accomplish and Binance had not explicitly confirmed that funds had been pilfered, but stablecoin issuers quickly froze funds Thursday evening.
“Our teams continue to work closely with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets,” Binance said in a statement posted to social media. “User funds are safe.”
Stablecoin providers Tether and Circle each said they froze funds Thursday in response to the incident.
Jeremy Allaire, co-founder and CEO of Circle, wrote on X that the company had frozen more than an equivalent of $800m in currency associated with the incident “in coordination with law enforcement”. Paolo Ardoino, the CEO of Tether, said on X that the company froze the equivalent of more than $1.5bn in currency related to “a potential Binance exchange hack”.
The price of bitcoin dropped 3.2% Thursday afternoon to under $79,000.
Binance was founded in 2017 by Changpeng Zhao, who in 2023 pleaded guilty to a felony related to his failure to prevent money laundering on the platform and stepped down as CEO. Donald Trump pardoned him in 2025.
Zhao posted on X on Thursday that “User funds are safe!” but added that the incident “does look like a hack on Binance”. He added that while he doesn’t manage Binance anymore, “as a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered”.

articles.content_orig:
A conference discussing the field known as ‘area studies’ said it was necessary to move beyond Western frameworks
Chinese academic courses designed to deepen understanding of different countries or regions face a challenge in better informing policy and moving beyond frameworks developed in the West, a conference in Beijing has heard.
Speakers said that as the country’s international engagement deepened, it needed a better understanding of the nations it engaged with, including their political systems, histories and strategic priorities.
The discipline – known in China as “area studies” – draws on disciplines including history, politics, economics and sociology to examine individual countries and regions.

articles.title_orig: With all votes counted, Netanyahu’s bloc has 53 seats, Eisenkot’s 48, Arab parties 19
articles.title_zh: With all votes counted, Netanyahu’s bloc has 53 seats, Eisenkot’s 48, Arab parties 19
articles.content_orig:
For decades, many Palestinian citizens of Israel stayed away from the polls, refusing to legitimize a system they say has oppressed their people, sidelined their concerns, and failed to represent them.
But this time felt different: after four years under the most right-wing government in Israel’s history, hundreds of thousands of Arab voters decided they could not afford to sit on the sidelines.
They turned out in record numbers – nearly 80% – to vote on Tuesday, compared with 53% in the last elections, according to the Mossawa Center, a civil society organization promoting equality for Palestinian citizens of Israel. That turnout gives Israel’s Arab parties unprecedented political sway with 19 seats in the 120-seat parliament.
That surge was driven by a number of interlocking reasons. First, rising violent crime in the Arab community – seen as the result of negligent policing. Second, an urgent desire to oust Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and bring an end to his right-wing coalition, which includes hardline ministers such as Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich. No one was left in any doubt about the strength of feeling towards Israel’s national security minister, in particular, on Tuesday night, as chants of “Ben-Gvir, go home” broke out at the election headquarters of Joint List, the major Arab political alliance, as it became clear just how well the party had done.
Netanyahu’s coalition has overseen Israel’s devastating three-year war in the Palestinian enclave of Gaza, which has killed tens of thousands, and a yearslong campaign of settler violence in the occupied West Bank.
“Our community wanted to bring down this criminal government, to change the grave reality caused by the policies of Netanyahu, Smotrich and Ben-Gvir,” said Dr. Ahmad Tibi, a leader of the Joint List.
Tibi has spent nearly three decades urging the Arab community to exercise their right to vote. Now, he said, that high turnout is already having an impact: keeping Netanyahu from forming another right-wing government.
Palestinian citizens of Israel – who make up 20% of the population – are descendants of Palestinians who were not expelled or forced to flee their homes when Israel was established in 1948. They were given citizenship but lived under military rule until 1966; many, though, feel that discrimination within Israeli society has continued to this day.
They also include Palestinians who were born before 1948, like Mohammed Abdelhai’s 80-year-old aunt.
On Tuesday, at her nephew’s urging, she became a first-time voter in the town of Tira, in central Israel.
“I told her we have to vote,” Abdelhai said. “The last government was very aggressive with us, so this time we need every vote,” he said.
The most important issue for him, he said, was a pervasive racism and lack of equality between Arabs and Jews in Israel.
“If we can make a change, we can make a change. Why not? Why stay stuck in the same place?”
The strength of the Arab vote also means that neither Netanyahu’s governing coalition nor the opposition bloc are expected to win an outright majority.
Now, Tibi’s Joint List, along with Ra’am, another Arab-majority party, appear to hold the balance of power.
Tibi said the Joint List is prepared to help the opposition form a minority government, led by former military chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot. The Joint List would not join the government and would not seek any ministerial appointments in exchange – only a commitment to combat crime impacting the Arab community and stop the demolitions of Bedouin homes, which have risen under Netanyahu’s government.
“If they want us to help, we will be there in order to help … we want to support the candidate of the opposition.” Tibi said.
But doing so will require Eisenkot and his coalition to “be brave” in the face of Netanyahu’s condemnation of any attempt to form a government with the help of Israel’s Arab parties, he said.
That’s because the idea of forming a government with the support of Arab parties has become politically toxic in Israel, with a majority of Jewish voters opposed. Several opposition parties have also previously ruled out such an arrangement.
It remains unclear how much Eisenkot is willing to lean on the Arab parties for support. The only opposition party that supports doing that is the left-wing Democrats Party led by Yair Golan.
“We have an opportunity to form a change government in partnership with Israel’s Arab citizens,” Golan said on Wednesday. “Now we need courage. We need leadership. We need to stop being afraid and to start taking action.”
For Tibi, it’s more than fear holding some political leaders back.
“It’s the pure racism against 20% of the population, Arab citizens. We are a legitimate part of parliament. We are a legitimate part of the citizens,” he said.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has consistently sought to delegitimize Arab voters and has repeatedly used the prospect of lawmakers from the Arab community sitting in government as a way to motivate his base to turn out and vote.
In September, the CEC approved a motion to ban Arab parties to run in the election – a decision that was overturned by the High Court.
As it became clear just how well Arab parties had polled on Wednesday, Netanyahu’s Likud issued a statement accusing them of “stealing the election.”
This was followed on Thursday by the chair of Israel’s Central Elections Committee (CEC) sending a letter to the head of Israel’s security agency, the Shin Bet, asking him to investigate allegations of foreign interference in the election aimed at boosting turnout among Arab voters.
In the letter, the CEC chair, Noam Sohlberg, admitted he could not attest to any of the suspicions, and Israeli police have said they have received nothing to back up the claims.
Arab party leaders say Likud’s attacks amount to incitement and have pledged to defend the election results. Mansour Abbas, Ra’am party leader, said he would cooperate with any investigation and Joint List chairman Yousef Jabareen said Netanyahu was “defeated” and “refuses to accept the voters’ decision.”
Many of the policies that have afflicted Palestinian citizens of Israel have been enacted under Ben-Gvir, the national security minister who was previously convicted of supporting terrorism and inciting anti-Arab racism.
On Tuesday, some residents in Arab-majority towns told CNN they left polling stations without voting because of intimidation from men supporting far-right Israeli parties like Ben-Gvir’s.
“People face high pressure – there was an old woman who could not stand the pressure, another one is pregnant who could not bear the situation and left … this is all because of racism,” said Taibeh resident Ulfat, who asked to be identified by her first name only.
From Tibi’s point of view, the higher turnout among Arab voters compared with the Jewish majority shows that Palestinian citizens are “willing to influence and take part” in Israeli politics.
“We are being blocked by the right and sometimes by the opposition. This is not a democracy. It’s an ethnic democracy. It’s a democracy for Jews,” he said.
That sense of exclusion was echoed by voters across Arab communities, many of whom said it is what pushed them to the polls this time.
Tira resident Munther Mansour, 60, has voted in the past, but this time he sees a real chance that his vote will count.
“We never took an interest in elections before. But the level of racism and changes in our day-to-day life forced people to go out and exercise their right,” he said.
“We belong to this country; we are part of the country. So we must exercise this right.”

articles.title_orig: Polymarket Is Investigating Suspicious Bets on Israeli Election
articles.title_zh: Polymarket Is Investigating Suspicious Bets on Israeli Election
articles.content_orig:
Prediction market operator Polymarket is investigating a string of well-timed and profitable trades on Israel's election this week, according to a Bloomberg News report on Thursday.
Shortly before polls closed on Tuesday, hundreds of newly created accounts placed bets on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu retaining his position and his Likud party winning the most seats, according to the report.
The report said those trades quickly became profitable- and together some of the accounts already cashed out over $100,000 - after some exit polls showed that Netanyahu’s party had won more seats than early reports suggested.
Many wallets have significant gains that have not yet been realized, the report said.
Prediction markets face growing scrutiny over potential insider trading, with platforms such as Polymarket and Kalshi reporting a surge in suspicious activity amid a sharp increase in trading volumes. Reuters reported in May that Polymarket had seen a significant uptick in trades flagged as suspicious this year.
Polymarket is reviewing dozens of newly created wallets that traded on the election , its internal investigative team told Bloomberg.
Data analysis firms Polysights and Bubblemaps have also flagged the activity as suspicious and are investigating, the report said.
The findings are not conclusive, and it can be difficult to distinguish potential insider trading from original research or lucky bets, Bloomberg reported.
Representatives for Polymarket and Polysights did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Bubblemaps said its analysis shared with Bloomberg was recent and that it had no further updates.

articles.title_orig: Israel’s election ended in deadlock. Here are four ways out
articles.title_zh: Israel’s election ended in deadlock. Here are four ways out
articles.content_orig:
Israel faces weeks, possibly months, of political limbo after final results show there’s no clear winner in its elections .
Neither of the two main blocs – one led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing Likud party, the other led by the centrist Yashar party of his main rival, Gadi Eisenkot – have reached the required 61-seat majority to form a government in Israel’s 120-seat parliament.
So how could a new government be formed?
Certainly, it does not look easy, with deep-rooted political and ideological divisions making any seemingly straightforward coalition almost impossible.
Still, it can be done, even if the result is a tenuous alliance that survives little more than a year or so in office. If party leaders are unable to figure it out in the 12 weeks they will have available, then Israelis will be back at the polls.
Here’s some potential scenarios that could avoid that.
On paper, the opposition’s surest path to unseat Netanyahu is built on Jewish-Arab cooperation. And that is its biggest obstacle.
Two of the opposition bloc’s right-wing party leaders, former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett and former Defense Minister Avigdor Liberman, oppose any government that depends on the two Arab parties in parliament – the Joint List and Raam – whether it’s from inside the coalition, or as outside supporters of a minority government. The two leaders have hardened their positions since the Hamas-led attack of October 7, 2023.
Only one government in Israel’s history has enjoyed the full participation of an Arab party. Raam was part of an eight-party coalition that succeeded in ousting Netanyahu in 2021, but it collapsed just after a year in office.
Even without forming a government, the opposition parties could still work together and leverage their parliamentary majority to replace the Knesset speaker, along with other key positions, and thereby constrain Netanyahu’s caretaker government as it continued in power. But the prospects of assembling a coalition to replace him as Israel’s leader remain highly complicated and politically charged.
Another option would see the implosion of the two blocs in favor of a unity government. Netanyahu’s Likud party would certainly be involved, along with some of his existing coalition partners, as well as – crucially – at least one party from the opposition bloc.
Netanyahu, in this case, is believed to be willing to part ways with his far-right National Security Minister Ben-Gvir – but not from far-right Finance Minister Bezazel Smotrich and the ultra-Orthodox parties.
Eisenkot , however, has ruled out sitting with Netanyahu, and it would be seen by many Israelis desperate to see the back of ‘Bibi’ as an act of betrayal if he were to change his mind.
Another scenario could see Netanyahu encouraging defections from opposition parties or individual lawmakers.
But all four opposition bloc party leaders – Eisenkot, Bennett, Liberman and Yair Golan – have declared they will not sit with him. And with Netanyahu’s bloc a full eight seats short, persuading eight individual defectors sets a high bar.
While all these possibilities are being discussed in the background, Israeli President Isaac Herzog will hold a very public round of consultations with the leaders of the parties that have made it into parliament.
Once he has solicited their opinions, he will task one of those leaders with the job of trying to form a government. Arab parties are expected to voice their support for Eisenkot, so the Yashar leader could be asked to go first.
Whoever gets the nod will have 28 days to complete the job, with a possible 14-day extension if needed.
If it all comes to nothing, the president will ask a second leader to have a go. They get 28 days only to sort it out.
After that, a majority of Knesset members could ask the president to task a third candidate, who then has 14 days to build a coalition.
If none of these produce a breakthrough, there will be another election.
The person who appears best-placed to navigate this timetable is Netanyahu. As caretaker prime minister, he can afford to wait: If main rival Eisenkot gets the first shot – and fails – the mandate is likely to pass to him. And if he fails as well, the political deadlock seems certain to lead Israel to another round of elections – with Netanyahu remaining caretaker for months, until another government is formed.
A repeat election – which would happen no earlier than next spring – is a real possibility, as these results look set to return Israel to a state of political paralysis and what would be the seventh general election in eight years.

articles.title_orig: Polymarket temporarily suspends trading on international platform due to security incident
articles.title_zh: Polymarket temporarily suspends trading on international platform due to security incident
articles.content_orig:
Security incident linked to performance-monitoring tool spurred platform to halt trading for about an hour
Polymarket temporarily halted trading on its international platform on Thursday because of a security incident that compromised a third-party provider, the company said.
Trading was paused for about an hour and resumed on Thursday afternoon. The company has promised to fully reimburse any affected traders.
The prediction market platform said it halted trading “out of an abundance of caution” after identifying and fixing the issue affecting its international platform.
“We’ll make this right and are fully reimbursing all affected traders,” the company posted on X once trading had resumed.
Polymarket said it referred the incident to a law enforcement agency in the United Kingdom.
Reports have linked the source of the incident to DebugBear, a UK-based company offering website performance-monitoring tools.
DebugBear’s own website was unavailable on Thursday afternoon and the company posted on X that it was “impacted by an ongoing security incident”. It also advised clients who were using one of its products to remove the embed code from their websites. The company did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
It was not immediately clear to what extent traders using the popular prediction market platform were affected, or the breadth of the impact. The company said anyone who was affected “will be made whole”.
