Donald Trump promised Americans a “ patriotic” alternative to big tech when he unveiled the T1 smartphone in June 2025, however, the product reportedly failed to live up to expectations .
On Wednesday, October 28, Zack Nelson , a popular YouTuber known for gadget teardowns and durability tests, put the $499 handset through its paces.
He also compared it with a Taiwanese model released in 2024, explaining that the president’s offering looked “extremely suspicious.”
“Phone so bad it makes you remember the Epstein Files,” one netizen joked.
Nelson’s review video of the T1 had amassed 9 million views as of this writing.
Right from the start, the reviewer placed the handset alongside the HTC U24 Pro, a phone he already owned.
He pointed out that the two devices matched in overall size, the contours of their angled metal frames, the placement of the power and volume buttons, the notification lights, the USB port, the headphone jack, and the microSD card slot.
The T1’s 6.78-inch curved display also had the same resolution and 120 Hz refresh rate as the 2024 HTC model.
Scratch tests yielded similar results, with the first visible marks appearing at level six on a Mohs hardness pick, a tool used to assess a material’s scratch resistance.
More pronounced grooves emerged at level seven.
Nelson then opened up both handsets, revealing that their interiors were identical too, down to the number and placement of screws, the motherboard, and the battery.
The most striking moment, however, came when the reviewer swapped the motherboards between the two devices.
Both phones booted up immediately, further suggesting that they were built on the same platform and sourced from the same manufacturer.
“As a factory owner myself, this is super frustrating ,” Nelson said, adding that Trump’s claims of American manufacturing were “a slap in the face” to those who actually produce goods in the country.
Nelson also questioned the president’s claims of patriotism by highlighting a design flaw in the T1’s American flag.
The national symbol on T1 had 11 stripes instead of the standard 13, which represent the original colonies that formed the United States.
Pointing out the discrepancy, Nelson sarcastically suggested that the Trump Mobile branding might account for the missing stripes, “one red, one white.”
He then raised another concern about the image, citing Section 8(i) of Title 4 of the U.S. Code, which states that the American flag “should never be used for advertising purposes in any manner whatsoever.”
#Trump ‘s #phone has arrived: a regular plastic #device in a #gold tone that was supposed to have a metal finish. Users are complaining about the cloudy plastic. pic.twitter.com/efUiynFnGU
— Chris | MC 🐂🀄️ (@0xChrisAdaji) July 5, 2026
The U.S. Flag Code, however, primarily provides guidelines for displaying and respecting the banner. A violation does not automatically constitute a criminal offense.
Nelson, meanwhile, did not hold back from calling attention to Trump’s past legal troubles and alleged lies during the video.
Nelson’s first personal jab at Trump came while he was explaining why he had taken so long to review the device.
The creator admitted that he had been reluctant to purchase a phone associated with a “34-time felon” because it set off his “ scam-o-meter. ”
The figure referred to a New York jury finding Trump guilty on 34 felony counts of falsifying business records in May 2024.
Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images
Later, during the scratch test, Nelson noted that the T1 had sustained marks at levels six and seven, quipping that those were among Trump’s favorite numbers.
Another favorite, he claimed, was 38,000, which he cited as the number of times the president’s name appeared in the Epstein files.
The reviewer subsequently broadened his criticism to Trump’s political record, accusing him of making promises without following through. He argued that the president was still complaining about America’s problems after several hundred days in office, despite having promised to fix them on day one.

articles.content_orig:

Vladimir Putin has said that Russia ⁠is prepared ‌for a potential war with Europe in his latest sabre-rattling threat against the continent, though ‌he claimed Moscow does not ‌want one.
The Russian president said his country would support any steps aimed at restoring relations with European countries, as he commented on his phone call with the leaders of Norway and Finland, which took place on Tuesday.
But in a chilling threat, he said that if tensions were to escalate too far, there “would be no winners”.
"First of all, we are ready, but we want no war with Europe”, Putin said.
“And if anyone wants it, let them prepare, but right now they have not achieved their goal to inflict a strategic defeat on Russia.
“And if things go too far, there will be no winners at all. Let no one forget that."
Finnish president Alexander Stubb and Norwegian prime minister Jonas Gahr Stoere had held “frank and substantive” talks with the Russian president in a bid to influence the Kremlin’s position as the conflict in Ukraine rages on.
Putin said they had been right to make the call, despite criticism from some European capitals that the two were breaking ranks and protocol by speaking with Moscow directly.
Follow the latest updates on the Russia-Ukraine war here.
Stoere said he and ​Stubb had "stressed ⁠the importance of de-escalation,” and that both had voiced strong support for Ukraine.
But the move attracted criticism from their Nordic counterparts including Danish prime minister Mette Frederiksen as they urged Europe’s leaders to “stick together” on Ukraine.
Swedish prime minister Ulf Kristersson said other European leaders also said they were not informed of the talks.
Putin added that Moscow did not want the Baltic ‌Sea to face ​a situation similar ‌to ⁠that in the ⁠Strait of Hormuz .
He said Russia wanted no impediments to navigation in the Baltic Sea and added that restricting communication could lead to a situation similar to that in the Strait since the outbreak of the US-Iranian conflict in February.
"Does someone ⁠want the same situation in the Baltic ⁠as in the Gulf or the Strait of Hormuz?" Putin said.
"I don't know. ‌We don't want ​that, but we will respond ‌to any challenge."
Also on Thursday, the UK’s former chancellor Rachel Reeves urged Brussels to seize control of £175bn in frozen Russian assets to help Ukraine defend against Kremlin aggression in the face of “a desperate winter”.
In her first significant intervention since leaving government, the Labour MP told the European Union that “the time to act is now”, with Kyiv confronting a funding blackhole and Donald Trump seeking to pressure the embattled country “to cut a deal with Moscow”.
Earlier this week, defence secretary Wes Streeting said that Britain must be ready for war in 1,000 days as the government tells Britons to stock up on tinned food and bottles of water.
Writing in The Telegraph , Mr Streeting warned that the UK’s adversaries could be ready to attack the country in 2030.
A jet-powered Russian drone hit two trains stopped at a station in central Ukraine on Thursday, killing at least 13 people and injuring 10 others, officials said.
Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy described it as a “horrific attack” that struck passenger trains in Dnipro.
Moscow and Kyiv have observed the truce in and around the devastated occupied southern city of Oleshky since Tuesday, despite remaining locked in war since Russia’s all-out invasion of its neighbour more than four years ago.
Previous efforts to secure ceasefires either never worked out or the truces quickly fell apart.

Update: Monday, 26 Oct 1220Z: We are awaiting written confirmation from CDC, but we have been now told that this applies to crew also .
Original Briefing: From midnight on November 4, every flight departing for the United States will require that passengers have completed a new form, stating that they have not been to the D.R.C./Congo in the past 3 weeks.
For all operators, this presents a rather burdensome paperwork requirement, at very short notice. It applies to every aircraft arriving into the US, not just airlines.
If you are just getting started with implementing the process, the following are the official documents and sources. We have saved copies of the current forms here for members to make things easier, but check for any updates.
If you have any input on how this is affecting your flight operations, please let the team know. We are especially interested in hearing how you are implementing the process, if you are using a digital method, and anything you learn along the way. We will then be able to update members. Thanks!
Review the full New Ebola Rule Briefing in your members dashboard. Further updates and member feedback will be posted here.
Below are some of the member questions we have answered.
Is this just for African countries? Nope, the place you depart from for the US is not relevant. All flights, all origins.
What happens if the passenger HAS been in the Congo in the last 21 days?
Then CDC says they cannot travel to the US. There is a mandatory 3 week waiting period. CDC says that “You are considered to have been in the DRC if you were physically present in DRC at any time during the previous 21 days. This includes entering or traveling through DRC by air, land, or sea. Connecting through an airport in DRC also counts as being present in the country, even if you did not leave the airport or the plane. The 21-day waiting period is based on calendar days. Day 0 is the day you leave DRC, and Day 1 is the first full calendar day you are outside DRC. You may board a flight to the United States beginning on Day 22, provided you meet all other travel requirements. You will not be allowed to travel to the United States during Days 0–21.”

articles.title_orig: 'We're technically homeless': Residential cruise ceases operations
articles.title_zh: 'We're technically homeless': Residential cruise ceases operations
articles.content_orig:
More than 200 passengers, mostly Americans, are stranded in Cambodia after the operator of a luxury U.S. cruise ship that was on a continuous around-the-world voyage ran out of money due to skyrocketing fuel costs .
Villa Vie Residences, the Florida-based operator of the MV Odyssey, said the war with Iran quadrupled fuel costs and forced it to suspend operations on Tuesday.
CEO Mikael Petterson told CBS News in a phone interview Wednesday that Villa Vie Residences was paying an average of $700 a ton for fuel before the war broke out in late February. Since then, it has been paying anywhere from $2,000 to $3,000 per ton.
The Odyssey uses between 700 and 800 tons per month in fuel, Petterson disclosed.
"When you divide it over 300 people on board, it's just backbreaking," Petterson told CBS News. "And this has been going on for nine months. We've tried to do everything we can do."
In a statement, Villa Vie Residences said the per cabin fuel costs rose from an average of $1,800 per month before the war to between $6,000 and $8,000.
The company was unwilling to pass those rising costs on to its passengers, Petterson said.
The Odyssey launched in October 2024 for a continuous around-the-world journey. At the time, passengers could become residents of the ship by purchasing a permanent cabin for several hundred thousand dollars. Some sold their homes to do so. At the time, they were given a 15-year minimum guarantee of residency aboard the Odyssey.
The Odyssey attempted to counter the spiking fuel prices by slowing down its itinerary and spending five or six days in each port "hoping that things would come to a close in the Middle East," Petterson said, but it wasn't enough.
"For us, when our monthly expenses go up from $400,000 to $2 million, where are we going to get the $1.6 million?" Petterson asked.
The Villa Vie Residences CEO said that the ship ran out of money as it searched for a financial partner, and the plan is now to file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy.
"We've borrowed money, we've stretched our payrolls as far as we can, and we're at a point where it's just at a breaking point where we need capitalization," Petterson said.
Passenger Benjamin Schatz thought the MV Odyssey would be his forever home.
"Honestly, right now, I'm in denial and in shock, and I'm heartbroken," Schatz, a retiree, told CBS News.
CBS News met Schatz in April 2025 for a story featuring Villa Vie Residences. At that point, he had been living on the ship for about one year. On Wednesday, he was given just hours to pack up his life and leave.
Said Schatz: "There are people now who are homeless and who have very little money and don't know what they're going to do."

articles.title_orig: Dow loses 100 points, S&P 500 snaps 3-day advance as Alphabet and Caterpillar tank: Live updates
articles.title_zh: Dow loses 100 points, S&P 500 snaps 3-day advance as Alphabet and Caterpillar tank: Live updates
articles.content_orig:
Alphabet shares plunged the most since Google went public in 2004, dropping 13% on Thursday, wiping out roughly $500 billion in market cap.
In its earnings announcement late Wednesday, Alphabet reported negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion for the third quarter, compared to the $2.7 billion analysts expected. The Google parent maintained its full year capital expenditure guidance of between $195 billion and $205 billion.
Microsoft , meanwhile, traded largely flat as investors focused on the tech giants' latest spending and free cash flow numbers in the third-quarter earnings report.
Microsoft reported $45.2 billion in capital expenditures and finance leases during the quarter, which was 30% higher than a year ago, but below analyst projections of $50.67 billion. Free cash flow fell 27% to $18.63 billion but remained positive.
The earnings reports come as investors scrutinize AI spending plans of tech companies and are focusing on the returns on those investments.
"Microsoft is building out its architecture in a measured way and as such contains fewer surprises," Ben Barringer, global head of technology research at Quilter Cheviot, said on Thursday. "Alphabet, by contrast, saw its share price hit after hours as a result of a fairly messy set of results and a poorly handled earnings call" .
Alphabet's biggest source of revenue, search advertising, grew 12% in the September quarter to $63.35 billion, but missed analyst expectations, adding further pressure to the company's shares.
Philipp Schindler, Alphabet's chief business officer, said the impact on the search business was partly because of lower monetization within the company's AI Mode. He added that Alphabet is now "scaling" ads within its AI Overviews and AI Mode products, including in international markets.
Google's search business has faced headwinds from the rise of other AI chatbots like OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude. People may be carrying out more search queries outside Google. Gemini, Google's own AI chatbot, has failed to keep pace.
"The problem for Google is it faces an innovator's dilemma and doesn't know whether to protect its core business or look to join the disruption. As such, Google has lost its edge with Gemini and is behind peers on agentic AI," Barringer said.
Google's dominant market share in the search business, however, could ultimately give it a leg up over its peers, Rosenblatt Securities analyst Scott Devitt said.
"I don't think it's a sea change," Devitt told CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" on Thursday. "If it's a problem for Alphabet, it's a problem for any consumer-facing AI agent or LLM as well. And so, it's a problem that I think is ultimately going to be resolved. And when it does, Alphabet, with its 4 billion search customers that become AI customers, is in an enviable position."
- CNBC's Robert Hum, Samantha Subin, Jordan Novet and Caleigh Keating contributed reporting.

articles.title_orig: Rivian Beats Estimates as R2 SUV Becomes Its Top-Selling EV
articles.title_zh: Rivian Beats Estimates as R2 SUV Becomes Its Top-Selling EV
articles.content_orig:
Rivian Automotive beat Wall Street's third-quarter earnings expectations as it ramped up production of its new R2 entry-level SUV that the company has promised investors will lead it to profitability.
Here's how Rivian performed in the period ended Sept. 30, compared with average estimates compiled by LSEG:
Shares of Rivian were up roughly 7% during afterhours trading Thursday, after hitting a new 52-week low of $11.38 earlier in the day. The stock closed at $11.45 a share, down 1.9%
The electric vehicle maker also revised its 2026 guidance to mark expected improvements in its vehicle deliveries, pre-tax adjusted earnings and capital expenditures.
The new guidance calls for a pre-tax adjusted loss of between $1.75 billion and $1.85 billion — a $100 million improvement at the midpoint from its prior guidance — vehicle deliveries of between 67,000 and 70,000 units, up from at least 65,000; and capital expenditures of between $1.4 billion and $1.5 billion, $300 million less at the midpoint.
Rivian attributed the improvement in its pre-tax adjusted earnings guidance to better-than-expected revenue related to its sales of regulatory credits, an IEEPA tariff refund receivable in the third quarter and its expected increase in vehicle deliveries.
The R2 — the first deliveries of which arrived to customers in June — has become Rivian's best-selling model and was responsible for "much of the gain quarter-over-quarter," the company said.
Rivian delivered a record 19,248 units from July through September. The company does not disclose deliveries by vehicle.
The EV maker remains unprofitable overall but continued to narrow its losses during the quarter. The company reported a net loss attributable to common stockholders of $913 million, compared with a loss of $1.17 billion during the third quarter of 2025.
Rivian's gross profit, which is closely monitored by investors, was $176 million during the third quarter, up from $24 million a year earlier. Its adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization was a loss of $435 million, a $167 million improvement from the same period last year.
The company reported that its software and services segment continues to grow, generating $605 million in revenue and a gross profit of $256 million, a 42% margin. That compares to its automotive operations, which recorded nearly $1.55 billion in revenue and a gross loss of $80 million.
Also on Thursday, Rivian reiterated that it expects the R2, a smaller and less expensive sibling to its current luxury R1S SUV, to have a positive gross margin by the end of the year. CEO RJ Scaringe has said the company needs to scale beyond current R2 production plans of 160,000 units in order to achieve overall profitability.
"That ramp-up is critical for us getting to positive gross margin on R2 and that ultimately will contribute to positive gross margin for the business," Scaringe told CNBC's Phil LeBeau during an interview Thursday. "We're going to see that through the end of the quarter and the unit economics will continue to grow … into Q1 of next year as well."
Rivian on Thursday said its cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments balance was $5.5 billion, up from $5.3 billion to end the second quarter.

articles.title_orig: Opinion | Can Canada, UK and Australia grasp chance offered by US-China rivalry?
articles.title_zh: Opinion | Can Canada, UK and Australia grasp chance offered by US-China rivalry?
articles.content_orig:
As the US shifts away from its commitment to global primacy, these Anglosphere nations have the potential to be a pivotal force for global stability
As middle powers, Australia, Britain and Canada can do more than most other nations to influence global peace in the face of a new great power rivalry between China and the United States. These three nations owe their citizens, and perhaps the wider world, an earnest effort to rise to the challenge of being peacemakers.
They have three attributes in common that give them unique potential to be a pivotal force. First is their own shared histories as members of the Anglosphere and therefore close allies of the US. Second is the recent US impetuousness and erratic behaviour towards the three of them, which demands greater independence and balance in their international relationships. Third is their shared middle power status, affording them enough diplomatic, military and trade significance to have great influence.
Today, though, Australia’s, Britain’s and Canada’s results as agents for global stability are mixed.

articles.title_orig: Ukrainians recount torture at hands of Russia’s sadistic ‘Dr. Evil’: ‘You can’t call him a human being’
articles.title_zh: Ukrainians recount torture at hands of Russia’s sadistic ‘Dr. Evil’: ‘You can’t call him a human being’
articles.content_orig:
Surviving Ukrainian prisoners of war have given sickening accounts of their torture at the hands of “Doctor Evil,” a notorious Russian medic at the heart of Vladimir Putin’s modern-day gulag system.
Operating out of Russia’s penal facility No. 10 in Mordovia, southeast of Moscow, Ilya Sorokin, 35, has been charged with torturing at least 29 Ukrainian PoWs in absentia by Ukraine’s SBU security service.
One former PoW described how the sadistic doctor would order them to strip off before subjecting them to cruel and degrading acts.
“There were 30 of us, all naked, in a room. He asked who had asthma, tuberculosis, or anything else,” Serhii Doroshenko, a Ukrainian military doctor, told the Times of London .
“But if, God forbid, you mentioned any illness, then he would torture you personally, on top of the torture from the prison staff, because you were making extra work for him,” Doroshenko added, speaking from his hospital bed, where he is still recovering from his injuries.
Doroshenko, captured during a battle for the eastern city of Mariupol in 2022, spent more than 1,000 days in Russian captivity before his release last year in a prisoner exchange.
“He kicked us and hit us with a baton and a stun gun. He knows where it hurts the most, and he deliberately strikes you right there,” Doroshenko said.
He described how Sorokin allegedly reserved his worst punishments for captured Ukrainian medical personnel, over unproven claims that they had carried out medical experiments on Russian troops.
“This myth was spread by Russian propaganda. They told us that in Mariupol medics ran some biological experiments on Russian soldiers and colonels,” Doroshenko said.
“That they had cut off their testicles. This is bulls–t, of course, but we got beaten for this just as much as artillerymen and snipers,” he added.
Other PoWs described how Sorokin, also nicknamed Dr Shocker, would wear a medical mask and sometimes a balaclava with a skull on it during the torture.
“You can’t call him a human being. He started to wave the stun gun around and shocked me several times,” Ukrainian marine infantry officer Pavlo Afisov told RFE/RL.
“He said we were ‘stinking khokhkly [A Russian slur for Ukrainians]’ who did not deserve decent treatment,” Afisov added.
Sorokin is also accused of using a stun gun on Ukrainian PoWs if they failed to shout “Glory to Russian medicine!” or if they asked for help with heart pains, festering wounds, or even a toothache.
Ukrainian inmates were ordered to address Sorokin with their heads down and their hands behind their backs, although some caught glances at his face, Doroshenko said.
“To raise your face was to die, or to receive so many blows that you might not survive,” he said.
The European Union has imposed sanctions on Sorokin, citing his “inhumane and degrading treatment” of prisoners.
Sorokin has denied the allegations against him.
He is far from the only Russian medic accused of torturing Ukrainian PoWs.
Hundreds of former prisoners have recounted witnessing Russian medical professionals “directly participating in torture, ill treatment, and the degrading treatment of detainees,” as part of a new report, “The Anatomy of Torture,” by the Kyiv-based Center for Civil Liberties.

articles.title_orig: Sandisk Reports Another Big Earnings Beat. Investors May Have Wanted More.
articles.title_zh: Sandisk Reports Another Big Earnings Beat. Investors May Have Wanted More.
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Third quarter earnings season is in full swing this week, with corporate results dropping from Big Tech heavy-hitters Microsoft ( MSFT ), Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ), and Amazon ( AMZN ).
Read more: Follow Amazon earnings live updates here.
Aside from Big Tech, industries from oil to chips to pharmaceuticals will be represented, as Exxon Mobil ( XOM ), Intel ( INTC ), Boeing ( BA ), Ford ( F ), and Eli Lilly ( LLY ) also open their books.
It's shaping up to be another strong earnings season. According to FactSet data , nearly a quarter of S&P 500 companies have already reported Q3 earnings so far, with an overall earnings growth rate of 29.5%. If that rate holds, it will mark the third straight quarter of earnings growth above 25%.
Sandisk ( SNDK ) stock climbed in extended trading after solid across-the-board earnings and guidance beats.
Notably, Sandisk announced it will enact an eight-for-one stock split, effective Nov. 19.
This price reflects trading activity during the overnight session on the Blue Ocean ATS, available 8 PM to 4 AM ET, Sunday through Thursday, when regular markets are closed.
Here's what Sandisk reported, compared to analyst estimates compiled by S&P Global Market Intelligence:
Revenue : $11 billion, versus $10.7 billion expected
Earnings per share: $52.60, versus $47.15 expected
Fiscal second quarter revenue guidance: $12.2 billion to $12.6 billion, with a midpoint above the $12.23 billion forecast by Wall Street analysts
Fiscal second quarter adjusted earnings guidance: $55.00 to $57.00 (on a pre-split basis), with a midpoint above the Street's $53.30 forecast
The NAND flash memory maker has been a key beneficiary of the AI data center boom.
"We have started fiscal year 2027 with another quarter of strong performance, with robust and growing demand for our products driving outpaced growth in our data center business," CEO David Goeckeler said in a press release.
The stock has soared in 2026, but it's had a rocky few months as of late. Year to date, shares are up over 460%, but the stock has largely treaded water since July.
Reddit ( RDDT ) stock plunged 17% after hours. The company reported better-than-expected third quarter earnings and revenue, but investors were disappointed by softer-than-expected US daily active users and a subdued fourth quarter outlook.
Here's what Reddit reported in the third quarter, compared to analyst estimates compiled by S&P Global Market Intelligence:
Revenue: up 53% year over year to $895 million, beating estimates of $875 million
Global daily active users (DAUs): increased 12% year over year to 130.3 million
US daily active users: decreased 2% year over year to 50.7 million
International daily active users: i ncreased 24% year over year to 79.6 million
Earnings per share: $1.40, versus $1.33 expected
Q4 revenue guidance: $1 billion to $1.03 billion, lighter than the $1.04 billion forecast by Wall Street
Q4 adjusted EBITDA guidance: $480 million to $510 million, with a midpoint below the $509 million expected
Amazon ( AMZN ) reported third quarter results Thursday, missing on the top and bottom lines, sending the stock falling.
Follow live updates from the report and earnings call here >
Starbucks ( SBUX ) earnings beat expectations on Thursday, as the company looked to move beyond its turnaround plan to accelerate growth.
For the fifth consecutive quarter, the coffee giant posted better-than-expected same-store sales growth, up 7.2%, compared to Wall Street's expectations of 6.2%. That was driven by US sales, which were up 7.7%, with roughly a 5% increase in ticket sizes as customers spent more at Starbucks and roughly a 2% increase in transactions.
"We have a clear plan. We've been working the plan. And the plan is working," CEO Brian Niccol said in prepared remarks. He added that the company is "operating with greater consistency" and that more customers are going to Starbucks.
Adjusted earnings came in at $0.80, more than the $0.71 Wall Street forecast. Revenue fell short, at $9.1 billion, compared with the $9.2 billion the Street was looking for, reflecting the sale of Starbucks China business.
International sales fell short of Wall Street's expectations, rising just 0.9% compared to the roughly 3% growth the Street was looking for.
Intel ( INTC ) reported better-than-anticipated third-quarter earnings after the bell Thursday, but Q4 revenue outlook fell short of Wall Street's expectations on declining PC sales.
Intel stock fell more than 20% on the news.
In the fourth quarter, Intel is projecting revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, well below the $17 billion analysts expected.
Intel says the shortfall is a result of a worse-than-anticipated drop in PC revenue. The industry is contending with two overlapping factors at the moment: difficult comparisons to last year, when Microsoft ended support for Windows 10, forcing enterprises around the world to purchase newer Windows 11 systems, and the steady increase in PC prices, which is eating into demand.
Rivian ( RIVN ) reported upbeat third quarter results after the bell on Thursday and boosted its guidance, citing strong R2 sales.
Rivian reported Q3 revenue of $2.155 billion vs. $2.02 billion per Bloomberg consensus, up 38% from a year ago. Rivian posted an adjusted loss per share of $0.48 vs. $0.61, and an adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization) loss of $435 million vs. $575.9 million, narrower than the $602 million loss from last year.
Rivian also reported a gross profit of $176 million, up $152 million from a quarter ago, though the automotive segment remained negative.
Rivian stock gained on the news.
Crocs ( CROX ) stock soared 25% on Thursday to its highest price in over two years as investors cheered on a return to growth for the footwear company's HeyDude loafer brand and a brighter outlook for 2026 sales.
In the third quarter, HeyDude revenue increased 6.1% over the previous year to $170 million, marking the first sales increase in six quarters for the struggling shoe brand.
Crocs bought HeyDude for $2.5 billion in 2022, its largest acquisition ever. But the brand struggled amid excess inventory and discounting, causing investors to become fed up with lagging sales.
HeyDude makes up roughly 16% of Crocs' total revenue, while the flagship Crocs brand accounts for the remaining 84% of sales.
Caterpillar ( CAT ) reported and a record order backlog of $78.1 billion in the third quarter, but the stock fell 11% in premarket trading as Wall Street set a high bar and AI-related stocks broadly got hit.
The company has become a growing industrial AI play as its power generation business, which makes and services turbines, has gotten a boost amid booming data center construction.
Here's what Caterpillar reported, versus analyst estimates compiled by S&P Global Market Intelligence:
Revenue: increased 17% to $20.7 billion, in line with Wall Street estimates.
Adjusted earnings per share: $7.20, versus estimates of $7.03 per share.
Guidance: Maintained full-year outlook for sales to grow in the mid-to-high teens
Analysts may be down on the stock as they were hoping for raised guidance and a wider sales beat.
"Our third-quarter results reflect the durability of our end markets, with strong order rates and a record backlog," Caterpillar CEO Joe Creed said in the release. "Our team continues to execute our strategic priorities in a dynamic environment, positioning us for a strong year while delivering long-term value for our customers and shareholders."
Eli Lilly ( LLY ) shares jumped 4% in premarket trading as strong demand for the company's GLP-1 drugs Mounjaro and Zepbound boosted the company's third quarter results.
Here's what Eli Lilly reported, versus analyst estimates compiled by S&P Global Market Intelligence:
Revenue: up 39% year over year to $24.4 billion, versus estimates of $22.6 billion
Adjusted earnings per share: up 7% to $7.48, versus estimates of $6.35
Guidance: I

articles.title_orig: Hackers Swipe Millions From Polymarket Users in Latest Security Breach
articles.title_zh: Hackers Swipe Millions From Polymarket Users in Latest Security Breach
articles.content_orig:
Security incident linked to performance-monitoring tool spurred platform to halt trading for about an hour
Polymarket temporarily halted trading on its international platform on Thursday because of a security incident that compromised a third-party provider, the company said.
Trading was paused for about an hour and resumed on Thursday afternoon. The company has promised to fully reimburse any affected traders.
The prediction market platform said it halted trading “out of an abundance of caution” after identifying and fixing the issue affecting its international platform.
“We’ll make this right and are fully reimbursing all affected traders,” the company posted on X once trading had resumed.
Polymarket said it referred the incident to a law enforcement agency in the United Kingdom.
Reports have linked the source of the incident to DebugBear, a UK-based company offering website performance-monitoring tools.
DebugBear’s own website was unavailable on Thursday afternoon and the company posted on X that it was “impacted by an ongoing security incident”. It also advised clients who were using one of its products to remove the embed code from their websites. The company did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
It was not immediately clear to what extent traders using the popular prediction market platform were affected, or the breadth of the impact. The company said anyone who was affected “will be made whole”.

articles.title_orig: Subcutaneous Toripalimab Plus Disitamab Vedotin sNDA Is Accepted in China for HER2-Expressing Urothelial Cancer
articles.title_zh: Subcutaneous Toripalimab Plus Disitamab Vedotin sNDA Is Accepted in China for HER2-Expressing Urothelial Cancer
articles.content_orig:
China's National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) has accepted a supplemental new drug application seeking the approval of a subcutaneous formulation of toripalimab (Loqtorzi; JS001sc) in combination with disitamab vedotin (Aidixi) as first-line treatment for patients with HER2-expressing locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma. 1 The application covers tumors with a HER2 immunohistochemistry score of 1+, 2+, or 3+.
With this filing, the NMPA has now accepted applications for subcutaneous toripalimab across all 13 indications for which intravenous toripalimab is approved in China. The agency accepted applications for 12 of those indications in March 2026, making JS001sc the first domestically developed subcutaneous anti–PD-1 monoclonal antibody in China to reach the new drug application stage.
In May 2026, the NMPA approved intravenous toripalimab plus disitamab vedotin for first-line treatment of HER2-expressing locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma, marking the 13th approved indication for toripalimab in mainland China. 2 Toripalimab had previously been approved in China in 2021 for advanced urothelial carcinoma in the second line or later.
The regulatory decision for the frontline combination was based on findings from the phase 3 RC48-C016 trial (NCT05302284), which enrolled patients at 74 centers across China.
RC48-C016 was a multicenter, open-label, randomized phase 3 trial in which 484 patients with previously untreated HER2-expressing locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer were randomly assigned 1:1 to disitamab vedotin plus toripalimab every 2 weeks or gemcitabine plus cisplatin or carboplatin every 3 weeks. 3
Progression-free survival (PFS) by blinded independent review and overall survival (OS) served as dual primary end points, and secondary end points included objective response and safety.
At a median follow-up of 18.2 months, the median PFS was 13.1 months with the combination vs 6.5 months with chemotherapy (HR, 0.36; 95% CI, 0.28-0.46; P < .001). Additionally, the respective median OS values were 31.5 vs 16.9 months  (HR, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.41-0.73; P < .001). The objective response rate (ORR) was 76.1% (95% CI, 70.3%-81.3%) vs 50.2% (95% CI, 43.7%-56.7%).
Median duration of response was 14.6 months with the combination vs 5.6 months with chemotherapy. 2
Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse effects (AEs) occurred in 55.1% of patients in the combination arm and 86.9% of those in the chemotherapy arm. 3
Toripalimab is an anti–PD-1 monoclonal antibody that blocks the interaction between PD-1 and its ligands, PD-L1 and PD-L2, and also induces internalization of the PD-1 receptor. Disrupting this signaling helps restore the immune system’s ability to recognize and attack tumor cells. 2
Disitamab vedotin is a HER2-directed antibody-drug conjugate composed of a humanized antibody, a protease-cleavable linker, and the cytotoxic payload monomethyl auristatin E. After binding to HER2 and being internalized by tumor cells, the conjugate releases its microtubule-disrupting payload. The combination therefore pairs targeted cytotoxic delivery with immune checkpoint inhibition.
Evidence for subcutaneous toripalimab has been derived from the phase 3 JS001sc-002-III-NSCLC study (NCT06505837), which compared subcutaneous with intravenous toripalimab, each given with chemotherapy, in patients with recurrent or metastatic nonsquamous non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). 1 The study met its primary end point in November 2025. In an oral presentation at the 2026 European Lung Cancer Congress, investigators reported that toripalimab exposure with the subcutaneous formulation was noninferior to that of the intravenous version, with similar efficacy and safety.
JS001sc-002-III-NSCLC is an open-label, randomized, multicenter phase 3 trial comparing the pharmacokinetics, efficacy, and safety of subcutaneous and intravenous toripalimab, each combined with chemotherapy, as first-line therapy for recurrent or metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC. 4
Patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to subcutaneous toripalimab 360 mg or intravenous toripalimab 240 mg, each given every 3 weeks, along with pemetrexed and cisplatin or carboplatin for 4 cycles. Those whose disease had not progressed then received maintenance pemetrexed with their assigned toripalimab formulation, with total toripalimab treatment capped at 35 cycles.
The study’s primary end points were the observed serum trough concentration at the end of cycle 1 and the model-predicted area under the concentration-time curve from day 0 to day 21 of cycle 1. Secondary end points included ORR, PFS, 6-month PFS rate, disease control rate, duration of response, and safety, which was assessed through AEs and abnormal laboratory parameters.

articles.title_orig: Starbucks posts slight revenue miss, earnings beat in Q4 results as CEO says turnaround plan 'is working'
articles.title_zh: Starbucks posts slight revenue miss, earnings beat in Q4 results as CEO says turnaround plan 'is working'
articles.content_orig:
Rivian Automotive beat Wall Street's third-quarter earnings expectations as it ramped up production of its new R2 entry-level SUV that the company has promised investors will lead it to profitability.
Here's how Rivian performed in the period ended Sept. 30, compared with average estimates compiled by LSEG:
Shares of Rivian were up roughly 7% during afterhours trading Thursday, after hitting a new 52-week low of $11.38 earlier in the day. The stock closed at $11.45 a share, down 1.9%
The electric vehicle maker also revised its 2026 guidance to mark expected improvements in its vehicle deliveries, pre-tax adjusted earnings and capital expenditures.
The new guidance calls for a pre-tax adjusted loss of between $1.75 billion and $1.85 billion — a $100 million improvement at the midpoint from its prior guidance — vehicle deliveries of between 67,000 and 70,000 units, up from at least 65,000; and capital expenditures of between $1.4 billion and $1.5 billion, $300 million less at the midpoint.
Rivian attributed the improvement in its pre-tax adjusted earnings guidance to better-than-expected revenue related to its sales of regulatory credits, an IEEPA tariff refund receivable in the third quarter and its expected increase in vehicle deliveries.
The R2 — the first deliveries of which arrived to customers in June — has become Rivian's best-selling model and was responsible for "much of the gain quarter-over-quarter," the company said.
Rivian delivered a record 19,248 units from July through September. The company does not disclose deliveries by vehicle.
The EV maker remains unprofitable overall but continued to narrow its losses during the quarter. The company reported a net loss attributable to common stockholders of $913 million, compared with a loss of $1.17 billion during the third quarter of 2025.
Rivian's gross profit, which is closely monitored by investors, was $176 million during the third quarter, up from $24 million a year earlier. Its adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization was a loss of $435 million, a $167 million improvement from the same period last year.
The company reported that its software and services segment continues to grow, generating $605 million in revenue and a gross profit of $256 million, a 42% margin. That compares to its automotive operations, which recorded nearly $1.55 billion in revenue and a gross loss of $80 million.
Also on Thursday, Rivian reiterated that it expects the R2, a smaller and less expensive sibling to its current luxury R1S SUV, to have a positive gross margin by the end of the year. CEO RJ Scaringe has said the company needs to scale beyond current R2 production plans of 160,000 units in order to achieve overall profitability.
"That ramp-up is critical for us getting to positive gross margin on R2 and that ultimately will contribute to positive gross margin for the business," Scaringe told CNBC's Phil LeBeau during an interview Thursday. "We're going to see that through the end of the quarter and the unit economics will continue to grow … into Q1 of next year as well."
Rivian on Thursday said its cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments balance was $5.5 billion, up from $5.3 billion to end the second quarter.

articles.title_orig: Rivian (RIVN) Q3 2026 earnings: revenue up 38%, R2 now its best-seller
articles.title_zh: Rivian (RIVN) Q3 2026 earnings: revenue up 38%, R2 now its best-seller
articles.content_orig:
The mass-market R2 has quickly become the company’s top seller by volume, but high-margin software deals and the Volkswagen partnership are the real forces keeping the automaker in good financial health.
The mass-market R2 has quickly become the company’s top seller by volume, but high-margin software deals and the Volkswagen partnership are the real forces keeping the automaker in good financial health.
Rivian reported its third quarter earnings of 2026, providing us a closer look at the company’s financial health as it ramps up production of its all-important R2 electric vehicle — which is now, for the first time, outselling all of Rivian’s other EVs.
Rivian said it brought in $2.155 billion in revenue, a 38 percent increase compared to the $1.558 billion in Q3 2025. Of that amount, $1.55 billion came from automotive revenue, which is up 36 percent year over year. Comparatively, the company reported $605 million from software and subscription services, a 45 percent increase year over year. As EV sales slow down, the company is seeking to make more money from its digital products, including the Autonomy Plus package .
Automotive gross profits were on an upward trajectory, a sign that the company’s finances were improving as it delivered more vehicles. Rivian made $176 million in gross profit this quarter, a $152 million improvement compared to the same time last year. The company still lost $80 million in Q3 automotive gross profits, which is much better than the $130 million loss a year ago.
In other words, Rivian is losing less than it did a year ago because they sold more cars and made more money per vehicle. (Also, the company continued to sell pollution credits to other carmakers, and also received a tariff refund from the government — all of which was recorded as revenue.)
Rivian is losing less than it did a year ago because they sold more cars and made more money per vehicle.
Rivian brought in $256 million in profit in software and services, up $102 million from last year, with a strong 42 percent profit margin. Most of this cash came from licensing their tech to Volkswagen , alongside customer subscriptions for Rivian’s Autonomy Plus driving features. In many ways, Rivian’s tech partnership with Volkswagen and software sales are currently paying the bills, keeping the company profitable overall while it absorbs a lot of heavy upfront costs from launching the R2.
Earlier this month , Rivian reported a record sales quarter, with 19,751 vehicles produced and 19,248 delivered. That represents an 85 percent year-over-year increase in production and a 45 percent jump in deliveries. (For a direct-to-consumer automaker like Rivian, deliveries serve as a proxy for sales.)
Rivian doesn’t break down sales by model, so we don’t exactly how many R2s have reached customers so far. But the company said that the R2 is now the “best-selling Rivian vehicle by volume,” outselling the R1T and R1S, as well as the Electric Delivery Van (EDV).
“We had great results with R2 becoming our best selling vehicle by volume in the third quarter,” Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe said in a statement, ahead of the company’s earnings call this afternoon. “Customer and media feedback on R2 has been exceptional.”
The R2 was designed from the ground up to be Rivian’s higher-volume, mass-market offering — and by overtaking the company’s more expensive, lower-volume legacy vehicles, it seems to be doing just that. Still, the R2 isn’t bringing in the bulk of the revenue yet, as indicated by Rivian’s use of the phrase “by volume.” Most of the money is still coming from the VW partnership and its software division.
But that could change once Rivian starts shipping the more affordable versions of the R2 , like the $55,485 Premium trim (coming in late 2026), the $49,985 Standard Long-Range (early 2027), and the $46,495 Standard (late 2027).

articles.title_zh: Nvidia CEO reportedly targeted by an alleged Chinese spy
articles.content_orig:
Jensen Huang reported to have had close relationship with tech company executive suspected of passing intel to China
US intelligence agencies believe the Nvidia chief executive, Jensen Huang, has been targeted by an alleged Chinese spy who had done business with him, according to a new report by the New York Times.
Alice Huang or Huang Le, of no relation to the Nvidia CEO, is an executive at a Singapore-based datacenter company called Megaspeed. She had previously been suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China , prompting American officials to surveil and monitor her. Those officials have determined that she was acting as a Chinese intelligence asset, passing commercial information to Beijing, the New York Times reported, citing unnamed sources.
In the course of their surveillance, American officials determined that Alice Huang developed a close relationship with Nvidia’s CEO, according to the Times. Nvidia’s powerful chips serve as a cornerstone of the AI boom and have vaulted Jensen Huang into one of the most influential leadership positions in the industry. In that position, he has developed a close partnership with Donald Trump as the US government attempts to defend its position as a leader in AI development.
White House officials are reportedly alarmed by Alice Huang’s access to the head of Nvidia precisely because of the close relationship he has developed with Trump, according to the New York Times.
The Trump administration has imposed restrictions on exports of advanced AI chips to China as a matter of national security. Megaspeed’s Huang was suspected to have been helping the government get around those restrictions.
In a statement to the New York Times, Nvidia said there was nothing out of the ordinary about the Nvidia CEO’s interactions with Alice Huang.

“Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” the spokesperson said in a statement. Megaspeed and customers like it “receive ordinary business information – not sensitive Nvidia trade secrets – and zero information relevant to national security”.

articles.title_orig: Audio recordings reveal decisions made moments before deadly train crash in Spain
articles.title_zh: Audio recordings reveal decisions made moments before deadly train crash in Spain
articles.content_orig:
New audio obtained by Spanish media reveals that the operator of a stopped train called a control center to say she could not restart the train as another behind it sped ahead in its direction. The resulting crash of the two high-speed trains Wednesday killed at least 69 people and injured dozens more. As of Thursday, 67 passengers remained missing, according to Spanish officials.
Many questions remain about the failures that led to one of Spain’s worst transportation disasters in decades and whether something could have been done to prevent it. Audio recordings of communications between the train operators and staff members at a control center in Madrid shed light on the decisions made in the minutes before the trains collided.
Spain’s transportation minister, Óscar Puente, said Wednesday that a security system stopped working because of a computer malfunction, causing multiple trains on the line to stop at about 8:30 a.m. local time. With the computer system down, rail traffic was then handed over to the control center in Madrid.
At about 8:36 a.m., the control center authorized a state-owned Renfe high-speed train to resume its journey, without speed limitations, even though a stationary ‌train from the private rail company Iryo was on the tracks ahead, Puente said. An erroneous ​decision was ‌made ⁠to restart the ⁠Renfe train, breaking protocol, he said.
Audio obtained by Spanish media of the conversations between the operators of both trains and the control center sheds light on the series of decisions leading up to the collision at about 8:53 a.m., near the train station in Urda. NBC News has not been able to independently verify the authenticity of the audio.
After the computer system went down, the control center told the Renfe train operator to resume its journey “at normal speed,” according to an audio clip.
“At normal speed? OK,” the operator responded.
“OK, we’ll talk later,” the controller said before signing off.
Several minutes later, someone from the control center called the Iryo train to authorize it to also continue on its normal journey, according to an audio clip.
The operator of the Iryo train, which was ahead of the Renfe train, called back seven minutes later to say she had been unable to restart it. “I’m still stopped at the entrance signal,” she said, according to the audio clip. The control center told her to restart the train when she could and to call back if she had further problems, according to the audio. Several minutes later, the Renfe train ran into the back of the Iryo train.
The crash, the second deadly high-speed rail train collision this year in Spain, sent shock waves across the country. Until recently, the high-speed rail network was considered one of Spain’s crowning achievements. The crash came just weeks ahead of a major election in Spain, and it has led to criticism of the government and protests.
In January, a separate disaster on the same rail line killed 46 people. Several days later, a commuter train near Barcelona derailed, killing the driver and injuring dozens of other people.
Hundreds of emergency workers, firefighters, police officers and soldiers responded to the scene of Wednesday’s crash to rescue survivors and recover bodies. Cranes were brought in to move parts of the damaged trains later in the day.
Spain has the largest high-speed rail network in Europe for trains moving at more than 155 mph, with more than 1,900 miles of track, according to the European Union.
The identities of victims have begun to emerge.
Fátima Báñez, a former minister, was among those killed in the collision, according to the leader of Spain’s opposition Popular Party.
“She was a tireless woman, a loyal friend, and always committed to improving the lives of Spaniards,” Alberto Núñez Feijóo wrote in Spanish on social media .
Antonio Acedo, the driver of one of the trains, was also killed, according to the Izquierda Española political party.
“Antonio was an exceptional person, a kind, prudent, and dedicated man,” the party wrote on social media .
The country is observing three days of mourning after the crash.
Dirk Llorens, an American who lives in Madrid, said he and his wife were on the stopped train when, suddenly, “I was thrown just violently, just over my table.”
“Then the train started sliding, and I could see that the roof had opened, and there was dust flying out of the back,” he said.
People were panicking and did not know what had just happened, he said. Llorens thought the train had derailed somehow. He turned and saw that “everything was destroyed.”
Llorens said that as he and his wife tried to escape from the train, he saw people who had “smashed their face” during the impact, with bloody noses and cuts on their heads spewing blood.
He said that the crash occurred on a hill and that “we were all just trying to get out because we thought the train would roll on the hill and kill us.”
As more injured people escaped from the train, Llorens saw a man “come out completely full of blood, and he was just sitting on a tree, just completely collapsed.”
“I think people were so in shock. We were all in shock,” he said.
Those who were less injured began trying to help one another, he said, adding that soon afterward, a large group of paramedics and police arrived.
“You really never know what can happen in life — that makes you appreciate life but also understand that some things can happen at any time,” Llorens said.
He called for transparency from the Spanish government about what happened.
“The Spanish government really needs to put all their effort in making sure that something like that doesn’t ever happen again,” he said. “I don’t think I’ll take a train in Spain unless I see that they’re having big improvements in what they’re doing.”
Daniella Silva is a national reporter for NBC News, focusing on immigration.
Hernan Muñoz is a freelancer based in Spain.

articles.title_orig: EU seeks 'highest level' ties with Canada in Montreal summit
articles.title_zh: EU seeks 'highest level' ties with Canada in Montreal summit
articles.content_orig:
European Union and Canadian leaders are set to meet at a special Canada-EU summit to discuss critical policies like artificial inteligence (AI), climate, energy and ⁠security.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said on Thursday, ahead of the summit, which begins on Friday, that the EU will continue to explore Canada's prospects for becoming the bloc's first "associate member."
But despite her comments, the summit's declaration is expected to exclude the term "associate member," a move pushed by Germany and other members.
"Our idea is simple: it is an association without accession," Von der Leyen clarified. "We can build a partnership that comes closer to membership than anything we have done before."
"We both want to bring our relationship to the highest level possible," von der Leyen added.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney had said this week he wasn't concerned about the  "associate member" status, or "specific names" to be given to the new alliance with the EU .
"What matters is the difference that it will make to the lives of Canadians," Carney added.
Ottawa's quest for deeper ties to Europe is seen as a move to reduce its reliance on the US since President Donald Trump imposed tariffs on a range of Canadian goods .
Frederic Merand, political expert on EU-Canada relations at the University of Montreal, spoke to DW about how the summit serves as "political impetus" to improve the bilateral trade relationship and to free Canada of its reliance on the US.
"It's not going to happen, over time, overnight. And every time we move closer to the Europeans, we realize how dependent we are on the US and how also vulnerable we are to, for example, us retaliation," Merand said.
But he added that courting the EU is also part of a broader strategy "to reinvent the Canadian economy, to create a single market, to attract more investment," as well as to diversify our partnerships with China, India and also other parts of the world.
The EU is "a natural partner" to work with, Merand said, given its existing free trade agreement with Canada, in addition to the close historical and cultural ties between the two partners.

An EU official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told AFP that Canada and the EU sought to align policies in areas such as climate, energy and artificial intelligence, allowing Ottawa to participate in some EU programs.
Canada has critical minerals needed for green technologies such as batteries and wind turbines, something for which Europe normally relies on China.
But Canada is in need of major infrastructure investment to develop its mining industry.
There are hopes that the summit can result in a plan for the European Investment Bank to back Canadian critical mineral projects.
EU and Canadian leaders are also looking into a digital trade deal that can allow for faster and cheaper online transactions.
Additionally, Canada could be allowed to participate in the EU's Erasmus youth program, which allows university students to spend a semester abroad.

articles.title_orig: Israel election result shows no overall majority as vote count complete
articles.title_zh: Israel election result shows no overall majority as vote count complete
articles.content_orig:
Vote counting is complete in Israel’s elections with neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc nor the opposition winning a majority in parliament, Israeli media have said.
As the provisional results were being published on Thursday, opposition politicians met to explore options for a coalition.
With more than 99 percent of Tuesday’s ballots tallied, Netanyahu’s bloc held 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset while the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot secured 48 seats, Israeli outlet Haaretz reported. The Arab list parties, meanwhile, held a combined 19 seats, it added.
Both Netanyahu’s bloc and the opposition parties fell short of securing the 61 seats required for a parliamentary majority.
The final results of the Knesset elections will be certified and announced by Wednesday. Until that date, the results are subject to change.
Tuesday’s elections – the first since the October 7, 2023, attacks on southern Israel and the start of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza – were widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu’s premiership.
On Thursday, Eisenkot, who heads the Yashar party, met former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, who leads the Together party, to discuss ways to form a new government “as quickly as possible”, according to a statement reported by Israel’s Ynet News outlet.
Eisenkot also met Democrats party chairman Yair Golan, the only member of the opposition alliance to support forming a coalition with parties led by Palestinian citizens of Israel, while all other political groups have rejected any such union.
Golan met separately with Mansour Abbas, who leads the United Arab list, or Ra’am, which is projected to win seven of the 19 Arab party seats.
“This is a time for action. Our responsibility is not to miss the opportunity for change and the salvation of Israel,” Golan said in a post on X after his meeting with Abbas.
Al Jazeera correspondent Nour Odeh noted that “Eisenkot has an uphill battle ahead of him.”
The former military leader-turned-politician has pledged “not to ally himself or get into a partnership with the Palestinian Israeli parties”, Odeh said, reporting from the occupied West Bank because Al Jazeera is banned from Israel.
But given the fact that no political bloc has a majority, the Eisenkot-led opposition bloc cannot form a governing coalition without the support of Arab-led parties, she added.
Meanwhile, Netanyahu’s Likud party has continued to amplify unsubstantiated allegations that Arab-led parties had “stolen” the election, potentially with foreign assistance – claims that have been rejected .
The head of the Central Elections Committee, Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg, said “serious suspicions” of foreign interference had been brought to him in a letter to the Shin Bet security agency. Sohlberg said he could not verify the claims, but given their serious nature, he asked the agency to investigate.
Eisenkot accused Netanyahu of working to delegitimise the election results with his allegations.
In a video posted on his X account, Eisenkot said: “The days of Netanyahu using state institutions against Israeli interests for his personal needs are over,” adding that no “spin” can change voters rejecting his government at the polls.
“Benjamin Netanyahu is not satisfied with the results, no matter how much he has been saying that he won,” political analyst Xavier Abu Eid told Al Jazeera.
He added that while it seems unlikely the opposition could take advantage by overcoming differences with the Arab-led groups, there could be an understanding to replace the current speaker of the Knesset, who is close to Netanyahu.
“If there is a new speaker in the Knesset, … Netanyahu loses an important ally,” Abu Eid said, adding that this might give an opening for the opposition to “actually start passing legislation” against him.
Odeh said the next steps would involve negotiations between political groups after the Central Elections Committee announces and certifies the election results by Wednesday.

articles.title_zh: US War Secretary seeks stronger ASEAN ties as China, Indonesia begin joint training - VOA
articles.content_orig:

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
Prime Minister Mark Carney is set to host European leaders in Canada as he seeks to deepen trade ties with the EU amid Donald Trump’s ongoing economic hostility.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President Antonio Costa will join Carney in Montreal on Thursday for a two-day summit.
It is understood the talks will aim to deepen trade, defence and economic relationships as Canada looks to secure relationships outside of Washington.
EU officials said ahead of the talks that the proposed partnership with Canada could improve the relationship more than has ever been achieved with a non-European country.
Carney said Tuesday the summit would launch further negotiations over the next year. “It doesn’t matter about specific names or nomenclature,” Carney said.
“What matters is the difference that it will make to lives of Canadians, young Canadians in terms of opportunities to study, work and travel, our Canadian businesses in terms of new opportunities, Canadian researchers in terms of depths of opportunity, and Canada as a whole becoming a more independent, more sovereign nation, so we can live our lives as we choose.”
Carney has ruled out formally joining the EU, which would require Canada to align its laws and regulations with the bloc’s.
Canadian officials said Canada would not assume the EU’s membership-related budget obligations, although it could contribute to specific programs. Carney has said any enhanced partnership would face a vote in Canada’s Parliament.
The summit puts Carney’s vision for a new global order to the test. At the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, in January, he warned that the U.S.-led international order was breaking down and urged middle powers to unite against economic coercion.
Trump has suggested Canada’s proposed EU arrangement could be a “hostile act” and threatened tariffs on Europe if he considered it unfriendly.
Asked Wednesday about possible retaliation, a senior Canadian government official told reporters the closer relationship was not directed against the United States but reflected longstanding shared interests.
The summit is expected to launch an “Alliance for the Future,” a framework for closer cooperation on trade, defense, critical minerals, technology and research. Von der Leyen said the alliance would help Canada and Europe respond together to a world of growing rivalries.
The proposed relationship could include regular meetings between Canadian ministers and European commissioners and expanded opportunities for students through the EU’s Erasmus+ program, which supports international study and educational exchanges.
European commissioners and Canadian Cabinet ministers will hold sector-specific meetings, beginning with a business forum Thursday before formal leaders’ talks Friday. Officials hope to develop the broader partnership for possible endorsement in 2027.
Tobias Gehrke, a senior policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations, said the disagreement over terminology was unlikely to derail closer cooperation.
“There is no magic shortcut to rapidly reducing Europe’s and Canada’s reliance on the U.S. economy and military — not least since Washington might retaliate,” Gehrke said. “But the political window is now wide open to take a much bigger step than was previously conceivable.”
Canada has long looked to Europe to reduce its dependence on its much larger southern neighbor. “It was the idea of not being alone with the Americans that drove it,” said Robert Bothwell, a University of Toronto historian.
Carney has deep personal ties to Europe. The former Bank of Canada governor led the Bank of England from 2013 to 2020.
He chose Paris and London for his first foreign trip as prime minister rather than Washington, a break with tradition. He said the countries reflected Canada’s founding Indigenous, French and British peoples.
Daniel Béland, a political science professor at McGill University in Montreal, said Trump’s policies are accelerating Canada’s efforts to strengthen ties beyond the United States.
“The policies and rhetoric of the Trump administration are clearly pushing both Canada and the EU to imagine a world without strong U.S. leadership and to act accordingly,” Béland said.
Ottawa is reviewing plans to buy 72 additional American-made F-35 fighter jets and considering Sweden’s Saab Gripen as an alternative. Canada has committed to an initial 16 F-35s.
Canada is the only non-European country participating in the EU’s 150-billion-euro ($167-billion) SAFE defense procurement program, allowing Canadian companies to take part in joint European military purchases.
But deeper defense cooperation faces obstacles. Sundar said France is pushing for strict “Made in Europe” rules that could limit Canadian companies’ access to future EU defense spending, while Germany favors broader participation by countries outside the bloc.
He said negotiations over the EU’s next seven-year budget could matter more to Canada than anything announced in Montreal.
The two sides already have a sweeping free trade agreement, known as CETA, that eliminated most tariffs. Most provisions have been in force since 2017, although some EU member states have yet to ratify it.
The United States accounted for 71.7% of Canada’s merchandise exports in 2025. Carney wants to double exports to other countries over the next decade.
Canada and the EU are pursuing closer cooperation on digital trade and critical minerals, including possible European Investment Bank financing. Canadian officials said Wednesday they were exploring ways to stabilize mineral prices and encourage investment.
Gehrke said Europe’s growing trade confrontation with China is driving demand for Canadian critical minerals. Canada has the resources and mining expertise Europe needs, while Europe offers industrial demand, technology and capital.
Sundar said the shifting international order presents Europe with an opportunity to become a more influential global power.
“Trump’s predatory behavior is allowing the EU to position itself as an alternative geopolitical anchor,” he said.

Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now.
Disrupt doors open Oct. 13. Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW.
Reddit has long attracted millions of users to its site through Google, with many even appending the word “Reddit” to their search queries for better answers. But as search traffic dries up amid the shift to AI-powered search, Reddit is rethinking its relationship with the open internet. In its third-quarter earnings call on Thursday, the company announced it’s transitioning to a primarily “logged-in experience.”
The move is designed to protect its data from AI scraping, allowing the company to instead forge lucrative licensing deals with model providers. But just as important, such a shift could help Reddit to increase its revenue even as it faces daily active user declines in its largest market, the U.S.
Overall, Reddit’s global daily active users were flat quarter-over-quarter in Q3, reaching 130.3 million, while U.S. daily active users dropped from 53.2 million in Q2 to 50.7 million in Q3 and were down 2% year-over-year.
The company is not alone in seeing such declines; the shift to an AI-centered web has impacted most websites and publishers by now, leading to fewer click-throughs, as AI summaries provide answers that don’t require website visits and Google’s traditional “ten blue links” have reduced relevance. (The change is now even impacting Google’s bottom line , its earnings revealed.)
But at Reddit’s scale, the numbers associated with such a decline are enormous. The company said search traffic referrals dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average per week in October. It warned that if the trend continues, daily active users could decline to a low-double-digit percentage by next quarter. (To play that out: a hypothetical 10% to 12% decline could bring Reddit to roughly 115 million to 117 million daily actives, down from 130.3 million in Q3. That’s a huge drop!)
At the same time, Reddit has gotten significantly better at monetizing its audience even as its growth weakens. Revenue increased 53% year-over-year to $895 million, ahead of Wall Street’s expectations of about $875 million. Net income rose 74% to $283 million. Advertising revenue grew 54% to $847 million while nonadvertising revenue, which includes its AI data-licensing business, grew 35% year-over-year to $48 million.
And despite a 2% year-over-year decline in U.S. daily users, Reddit’s average revenue per daily active user in the U.S. rose 53% to $13.82. Globally, average revenue per daily active user increased 36% year-over-year to $6.87.
Shifting to a logged-in experience could boost those numbers even higher because logged-in users are typically worth more to advertisers.
Unlike the logged-out users who often find their way to the site via search, logged-in users provide more signals about their interests and behaviors, which helps to better target and personalize ads.
Those same signals would also help Reddit provide a more personalized experience to its users, which includes personalized feeds, recommendations of new communities to subscribe to, and pushes to vote, comment, participate, and more. (This also includes pushing recommendations to its new algorithmic “For You” feed, announced yesterday , which will combine posts from communities users belong to alongside other recommendations based on their interests.)
Still, a change of this magnitude could be the canary in the coal mine for the open web.
“I don’t know about you, but as someone whose life has been defined by the open internet, it’s a big change for me,” wrote Reddit co-founder and CEO Steve Huffman in a post published on Reddit’s site . “But I’ve come to the conclusion that this is the right decision for our platform and the right decision for our business,” he said.
The company notes that the shift to the logged-in experience will not be an overnight change; it will first run tests in select markets outside the U.S. in the fourth quarter. It doesn’t yet have a timeline for when the change will be rolled out to all its users worldwide. It also acknowledged that access to a logged-out front page is important.
Plus, Reddit pointed out that being logged in doesn’t mean having to give up anonymity, nor will it remove its option to browse anonymously through its “incognito mode” experience, which is being rebuilt.
“There are still plenty of questions that are unanswered, particularly around where the boundaries should be between logged-in and logged-out experiences,” Hoffman wrote. “This is a big evolution for Reddit, and not one we’re taking lightly. But I believe it’s the right next step for the platform and for our future.”

articles.title_orig: Reddit shares sink on weak sales guidance and plans login requirement test as Google search traffic shrinks
articles.title_zh: Reddit shares sink on weak sales guidance and plans login requirement test as Google search traffic shrinks
articles.content_orig:
Reddit plans to require all users to create official accounts to access the social media platform, marking a major departure for the site known as "the front page of the internet."
The company revealed the change Thursday as part of its third-quarter earnings, in which it beat on the top and bottom lines, but provided weak fourth-quarter sales guidance. The company's shares dropped over 15% after its numbers were released.
Here's how the company did compared with LSEG estimates:
Reddit CEO Steve Huffman told CNBC in an interview that the company's shrinking search-referral traffic from Google played a major role in its planned efforts to require people to become "logged-in" users.
A previous Google search update designed to surface "authentic" content from internet forums helped Reddit grow its user base over the past few years, but the search giant's continued push on AI overviews and related chatting features has negatively impacted referral traffic .
"I think fundamentally that relationship between Google and the rest of the internet is evolving, and so for us, this means a continued focus on our core users that come to Reddit directly," Huffman said.
Previous Google algorithm changes would "kind of come and go," Huffman said, but the company's AI efforts represent "a fundamental shift in how the Google product works, from being a traffic driver to whatever's going on now."
Huffman didn't provide any specific timing on when Reddit plans for the platform registration change, saying only that implementing it through the site would involve a lot of complexity . The company will begin testing in the fourth quarter outside of the U.S.
He said that Reddit is still determining what parts of the service logged-out users will be able to see, and will iron out the details as part of its upcoming testing.
Reddit said that daily active uniques, or DAUq, rose 12% year-over-year to 130.3 million in the third quarter, trailing Wall Street estimates of 133.7 million. U.S.-specific DAUq dropped 2% year-over-year to 50.7 million, which was below analyst projections of 53.5 million.
Huffman said that "search referral traffic is down meaningfully in this quarter" and that the trend will continue in the fourth quarter.
He said that Reddit is continuing its effort to make its platform "a daily habit" for users. "So that's where our focus is: growing those app users and logged-in users," Huffman said.
Reddit, which derives the bulk of its overall sales from online advertising, is able to monetize logged-ln users better than logged-out users , because those registered users are more active and valuable to advertisers itching to deliver more targeted ads.
"The vast majority of our revenue comes from our app users and logged-in users are direct traffic, and both of those are up Q. over Q. and so that's where our focus is," Huffman said.
The company's third-quarter sales grew 53% year-over-year, marking an end to the eight-straight quarters of revenue growth eclipsing 60% that it reported in July as part of its second-quarter earnings.
Reddit said that fourth-quarter sales will come in a range of $1 billion to $1.03 billion, which was below Wall Street estimates of $1.05 billion.
"It's still a strong guide," Huffman said about its revenue guidance. "We are still growing at an industry leading rate, and that's despite the headwinds from search referrals."
Reddit's third-quarter average revenue per user, or ARPU, came in at $6.87, which was higher than the $6.50 that analysts were expecting.
The company's "other revenue" segment, which includes its data-licensing business, jumped 35% year-over-year to $48 million in the third quarter. Reddit's two biggest data-licensing partners are OpenAI and Google.
Huffman said that Reddit remains "in negotiations" with Google over its data-licensing agreement, and said that it is "only going to do a deal that makes sense for Reddit," if it chooses to continue the partnership.
"I think there's a lot of strategic considerations that goes into that," Huffman said.
Huffman called the required registration plan a "big change" for himself, considering he "grew up on the open Internet."
"Reddit is the last platform to provide basically unfettered logged-out access, and that's largely because of me, I've been holding that line," Huffman, a Reddit co-founder, said. "I think users will probably go through the same understanding that I have, which is that it's a sign of the times. It's an evolution of how these platforms work."
Huffman later expanded on the significance of AI's impact on Reddit's user growth in an earnings call with analysts, and explained that the company plans to continue spending on marketing efforts intended to offset search-referral declines. "This is a consequential time for Reddit, and this period does remind me of about 11 years ago when I came back to the company," Huffman told analysts, referring to when he rejoined Reddit in 2015 following it's then-chief Ellen Pao stepping down. "We had a lot of conversations then about what is Reddit and what is Reddit for, and what is our place in this ecosystem. And we've been having those conversations at Reddit recently." "Reddit's mission is to create community and belonging for everyone in the world, and while there's overlap between Reddit and other players in the ecosystem, whether we're talking about social media or AI search, fundamentally, Reddit is communities and conversations," Huffman said.
